Bounded process-event wire contract shared by the native owner and plan checker.
All values in engage() must share a single plan time; only gear.engage changes the live relation.
A declared channel's safe value MUST be release(). Device-owned queues reject this host feature.

types.name: GearTerm
types.doc: SI encoder timing and count size, explicitly supplied by the installed controller/driver.

types.name: ProcessChannelDeclaration
types.doc:
Deployment output channel with a mandatory safe value. Faults and emergency stops always take it
there; a channel that `keepOnStop`, such as a gripper's or vacuum's, keeps its output through a
commanded stop or an aborted motion, so a robot that stops does not drop what it holds.

types.name: ProcessEventCodec
types.doc: ASCII ABI encoding shared by plan submission, blueprint and event polling.

types.name: ProcessEventValue
types.doc: Runtime output value, independent of the MotionKit authoring package.

types.name: ProcessTimedEvent
types.doc: Output change scheduled in plan-relative trajectory time.

types.name: SegmentArrays
types.doc:
A run of polynomial segments held as arrays in native memory, such as a
MotionKit plan's, for an in-process runtime to read in place. Segment `i`
starts `starts[i] - starts[0]` after the run's start, lasts `durations[i]`,
and has degree `degrees[i]`. The arrays' joints are source joints: source
joint `j` drives robot joint `jointMap[j]`, with its coefficient of power `p`
at `coefficients[(i * jointMap.length + j) * STRIDE + p]`. A robot joint no
source joint drives follows its leaders when `couplings` couple it to some
(the sum of their terms), as the runtime does, and otherwise holds its `heldPositions` value.

The spans are borrowed: they stay readable while their owner is open, so a
submission carrying them is consumed while its plan is alive. `segments()`
copies them into `TrajectorySegment`s for robots that need managed values.

fields.name: STRIDE
fields.doc: Coefficients stored per joint and segment: degree zero through five.

fields.name: robotJointCount
fields.doc: The robot joint count the segments drive.

fields.name: slice
fields.doc: Segments `[first, last)`, reading the same memory.

fields.name: coefficient
fields.doc: Robot joint `joint`'s coefficient of `power` in segment `index`.

fields.name: robotValues
fields.doc:
Source joints' `values` over every robot joint: each at its robot joint, a
coupled joint's from its leader (with the coupling's offset when the values
are `positions`, not their derivatives), and `rest` for every other joint.

fields.name: robotTolerances
fields.doc:
Source joints' tolerances over every robot joint: as `robotValues`, but a
coupled joint's is its leaders' scaled by the sizes of the ratios and summed, so it
allows the same error, and `rest` for every other joint.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: The segments as managed values over every robot joint, timed from the first one's start.

types.name: TrajectorySegment
types.doc: One joint-space polynomial segment, in seconds from its start knot.

types.name: RobotKinematics
types.doc:
Compiles a `RobotModel` into a `kinematicskit.KinematicModel`. Compiled
IDs are the robot's own: body IDs are `LinkId`s, joint and DOF IDs are
`JointId`s, frame IDs are `FrameId`s. Joints follow ARCHITECTURE.md's
joint-frame convention: `child = parent · parentFrame · motion · childFrame⁻¹`.

types.name: FrameTransform2
types.doc: Static planar transform: child frame pose expressed in the parent frame.

types.name: FrameTree2
types.doc: Tree of static planar frame transforms with explicit target/source direction.

fields.name: fromRobotModel
fields.doc:
Builds planar transforms for model frames attached to one body link.
Frames on other links are omitted; resolving them requires link kinematics.
The model frame's z translation is ignored, but roll or pitch is rejected.

fields.name: add
fields.doc: Adds one parent-child edge; each child may have only one parent.

fields.name: lookup
fields.doc: Returns `target_T_source`: the source frame pose expressed in target coordinates.

fields.name: transformPose
fields.doc: Transforms a pose expressed in source coordinates into target coordinates.

types.name: GnssPoseLocalization
types.doc:
Converts a dual-antenna GNSS pose fix into a local ENU frame.

Sensor values are latitude degrees, longitude degrees, and ENU yaw radians,
as published for a `gnss_pose` sensor. The configured antenna pose is the
antenna origin expressed in the robot body frame. Altitude is intentionally
ignored by this planar localization service. A fix is used while it lies
within `maximumAgeNs` of the robot snapshot, measured on its source clock
when that matches the snapshot's, or else on the shared local receive clock;
a fix from an unrelated clock is ignored. Feed valid states to
`PoseFusionLocalization.fuse` to correct wheel odometry.

fields.name: fromRobotModel
fields.signature: (model:RobotModel, sensorId:String, bodyLinkId:String, referenceFrame:String, bodyFrame:String, originLatitudeDegrees:Float, originLongitudeDegrees:Float, ?positionVarianceMetersSquared:Float, ?yawVarianceRadiansSquared:Float, ?maximumAgeNs:Float):GnssPoseLocalization
fields.doc: Builds the GNSS source and antenna lever arm from authored robot frames.

types.name: HolonomicOdometryLocalization
types.doc:
Wheel odometry for a three-wheel omni/kiwi base exposed as an `odom` to
`base` localization service, mirroring `WheelOdometryLocalization`.
`HolonomicDrive.createOdometry()` returns `null` because the common drive
interface is typed to differential odometry, so this takes the wheel
joints/geometry directly from the authored holonomic role.

types.name: Localization
types.doc: Service that derives a framed pose estimate from robot observations.

types.name: LocalizationQuality
types.doc: Qualitative confidence in a derived planar pose.

types.name: LocalizationState
types.doc: A pose estimate with explicit frame, uncertainty, and clock identity.

fields.name: pose
fields.doc: The pose of `bodyFrame` expressed in `referenceFrame`.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (sequence:Int64, pose:Pose2, referenceFrame:String, bodyFrame:String, covariance:PoseCovariance2, quality:LocalizationQuality, sourceTimestampNs:Int64, receivedTimestampNs:Int64, sourceClockId:String, receivedClockId:String):Void

types.name: PoseCovariance2
types.doc: Symmetric 3×3 covariance for planar x, y, and yaw.

types.name: PoseFusionLocalization
types.doc: Fuses wheel odometry with covariance-weighted external planar pose observations.

fields.name: fuse
fields.doc: Fuses an external pose observation after transforming both frames explicitly.

types.name: PoseFusionOptions
types.doc: Freshness, outlier, and recovery limits for pose fusion.

types.name: RobotFrameTree2
types.doc: Builds a current planar frame tree from authored robot kinematics and joint state.

fields.name: fromSnapshot
fields.doc:
Resolves model links and frames from one robot snapshot. The model and
blueprint must describe the same revision. Nonplanar link/frame poses are
omitted because FrameTree2 cannot represent roll or pitch.

types.name: SimulationTruthLocalization
types.doc: Projects an owned Simulation robot base pose into a map-frame estimate.

types.name: WheelImuLocalization
types.doc: Wheel displacement with heading increments corrected by the IMU gyro z rate.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `mountRotation` is the sensor's xyzw orientation in the body frame.

fields.name: fromRobotModel
fields.doc: Resolves the IMU and its mount from the authored model.

types.name: WheelOdometryLocalization
types.doc: Differential wheel odometry exposed as an `odom` to `base` localization service.

fields.name: rebase
fields.doc: Re-anchors wheel integration from a same-tick localization observation, retaining its uncertainty.

types.name: ArmSwivel
types.doc:
Where a redundant arm's swivel (elbow) angle is measured: a shoulder, an
elbow and a wrist point, each fixed on a link. The swivel is how far the
elbow is turned about the shoulder-wrist line, from the plane holding that
line and `reference` (a direction in the arm's base frame, base Z by
default), positive by the right-hand rule about shoulder -> wrist. On a
7-axis arm it is the one motion left once the tool pose is fixed, so it
names the arm's configuration (see kinematicskit `SwivelTask`).

fields.name: throughJoints
fields.doc:
The swivel through three joints' pivots (where each joint sits on its
child link): for a 7-axis arm, its 2nd, 4th and 6th joints.

types.name: ClearanceChange
types.doc:
A change to the cell during a program (COLLISION.md CL-D6, CL-D9),
declared with the program by whoever builds it: a grasp or a place, and
contact windows. Bodies are named as the clearance world names them.

fields.name: Attach
fields.doc: `body` rides on `link`; only the named collision objects may contact it.

fields.name: Detach
fields.doc: `body` stays where it is, fixed in the cell (a place).

fields.name: OpenWindow
fields.doc:
The pair keeps at least `margin` (an approach or a retract), or may
touch when `margin` is null (the contact itself), until the window
closes.

types.name: ClearanceScene
types.doc:
A clearance world whose cell can change while a program runs (CL-D6,
CL-D9): validation replays the program's changes in time order, with the
arm at `q` when each happens. `reset` returns to the cell as built.

types.name: ClearanceViolation
types.doc: Two bodies closer than they may be. `distance` is zero when they touch or overlap.

types.name: ClearanceWorld
types.doc:
What process planning asks of a clearance world (COLLISION.md CL-D12):
margin violations with per-body inflation, the closest pair, sampled
straight joint sweeps, and the motion bounds of its bodies, for an arm at
joint values. `robotkit.collision.CollisionClearance` implements it on a
collisionkit world.

Margins: a pair must keep `margin` (or a smaller `wanted`); with
`contact`, a tool body need keep only `contactMargin` from fixed bodies.
`displacements` (one per body) widen a pair's required distance by both
bodies' bound, as the continuous proof needs.

fields.name: group
fields.doc: The arm whose joint values the queries take.

fields.name: distanceBetween
fields.doc: Minimum signed gap of named objects or physical members, independent of pair exemptions.

fields.name: violation
fields.doc: The first pair closer than it may be at `q`, or null.

fields.name: closest
fields.doc: The closest checked pair, clear or not, or null when none is checked.

fields.name: sweep
fields.doc: The first violation along the straight joint motion, sampled at most `maxJointStep` per joint.

fields.name: closestSweep
fields.doc: The closest pair over the same sampled sweep.

fields.name: motionEnvelope
fields.doc: CL-D5's motion envelope of the bodies over joint boxes.

fields.name: displacementBounds
fields.doc: Per-body displacement bounds for joint errors at `q`.

fields.name: auditDisplacement
fields.doc: Checks the bound against an actual displacement; returns the largest ratio.

fields.name: withGroup
fields.doc: The same geometry on another compiled group (a worker's).

types.name: ExternalAxes
types.doc: External joints come from the include owning the nearest physical tool flange.

types.name: Grasp
types.doc: Selects a width-compatible pinch between opposite planar faces.

fields.name: find
fields.signature: (faces:Array<GraspPlane>, hull:Array<Vec3>, approach:Vec3, minimumWidthMm:Float, nominalWidthMm:Float, maximumWidthMm:Float, fingerLengthMm:Float, ?preferredWidthAxis:Vec3):GraspFrame
fields.doc:
Pick the opposing face pair nearest `nominalWidthMm`, with the approach direction perpendicular to
the pinch axis. The part's collision hull supplies actual extents and fingertip contact at the
far-side support plane after insertion; a grasp that does not fit the jaw range or finger length is refused.

types.name: GraspFrame
types.doc: A face-derived parallel-jaw grasp, in the part's local frame.

types.name: GraspPlane
types.doc: A planar face from the part's local CAD frame.

types.name: IKResult
types.doc: Outcome of one `Manipulator` IK solve; never thrown for non-convergence.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Why the solver stopped (see `kinematicskit.KinematicStatus`).

fields.name: rootPose
fields.doc: World pose of the robot's root after a solve that moved the base (`IkOptions.movingBase`); null otherwise.

types.name: IkMethod
types.doc: How `KinematicGroup.solve` runs.

fields.name: Tracking
fields.doc: Damped least squares: small, smooth steps from a nearby seed (tracking, dragging).

fields.name: Reaching
fields.doc: Levenberg-Marquardt: reaches far targets from a distant seed.

fields.name: Prioritized
fields.doc:
Hard tasks (the tool target, an exact swivel) as equalities, soft ones
(a posture, a swivel preference) as well as they allow: kinematicskit's
`PrioritizedSolver`. Chosen whenever a posture is preferred.

types.name: IkOptions
types.doc:
Settings for one `KinematicGroup.solve`. The defaults suit tracking a
tool-centre-point target from a nearby seed.

fields.name: positionAxes
fields.doc: Position axes in the target frame; 7 selects X, Y and Z.

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc: Hard orientation rows; an axis leaves spin about that local axis free.

fields.name: orientationPreference
fields.doc: Soft tool orientation, optimized only after the selected hard rows.

fields.name: damping
fields.doc: Damping of the DLS step (tracking) or the initial LM damping (reaching).

fields.name: atFlange
fields.doc: The target is the flange's pose, not the tool centre point's.

fields.name: swivel
fields.doc: A swivel angle to solve at (radians; see `ArmSwivel`); needs a swivel.

fields.name: swivelExact
fields.doc: Hold `swivel` exactly; otherwise it is a preference the tool target wins over.

fields.name: posture
fields.doc:
A posture the group is drawn towards (`q` order; external axes ignored):
the arm stays comfortable and the external axes bring the work to it.
Solved prioritized, so it shapes the configuration only; the tool target
is still met exactly.

fields.name: postureWeight
fields.doc: Strength of the pull towards `posture`, per radian (or metre) away.

fields.name: rootPose
fields.doc:
Move the robot's base as well (`KinematicGroup.baseMotion`): the robot
root's current world pose. The target is then in the world frame, and the
result reports where the base moved (`IKResult.rootPose`).

fields.name: baseCost
fields.doc: With `rootPose`: how much the base's motion costs against the arm's (> 0 lets the arm go first).

fields.name: held
fields.doc: Group DOFs (`q` indices) held at `heldValues` while the rest solve, e.g. a positioner at a chosen angle.

fields.name: freedom
fields.doc: Selects the hard tool task. Returns this.

fields.name: preferringOrientation
fields.doc: Prefers an orientation without adding any hard orientation rows.

fields.name: flange
fields.doc: Targets the flange instead of the tool centre point. Returns this.

fields.name: atSwivel
fields.doc: Solves at a swivel angle, held exactly or as a preference. Returns this.

fields.name: movingBase
fields.doc: Moves the robot's base too, from its current world pose; the target is then in the world. Returns this.

fields.name: reaching
fields.doc: Levenberg-Marquardt, for far targets from a distant seed. Returns this.

fields.name: preferring
fields.doc: Draws the arm towards `posture` while the external axes take up the rest. Returns this.

fields.name: holding
fields.doc: Holds the group DOFs `indices` (in `q` order) at `values` while the rest solve. Returns this.

types.name: JointGroup
types.doc:
An ordered, named selection of joints with their limits (e.g. an arm's
joints; see `Manipulator.group`). A joint whose limits have `lower >= upper` (the
`JointLimits` default, and the convention for unbounded/continuous
joints) is treated as unlimited and is never clamped.

fields.name: clamp
fields.doc: Clamps each value to its joint's limits; leaves unlimited joints (lower >= upper) untouched.

types.name: JointRoute
types.doc: Bounded, deterministic bidirectional joint-space search. The caller verifies directed motion edges.

fields.name: plan
fields.signature: (from:Array<Float>, to:Array<Float>, lower:Array<Float>, upper:Array<Float>, clear:(Array<Float>, Array<Float>) -> Bool, ?iterations:Int, ?step:Float):Array<Array<Float>>
fields.doc: Includes both endpoints. A failed bounded search is explicit, never evidence that no route exists.

types.name: KinematicGroup
types.doc:
The joints that move a tool, solved together: those from `rootLink` to
the link carrying the `flangeFrame` (a rail under an arm, then the arm),
and with a `workFrame`, those from `rootLink` to it (a positioner holding
the workpiece). Kinematics run on the whole robot compiled by
`RobotKinematics`, so joint couplings apply; robot DOFs outside the group
stay at their defaults.

Every pose, Jacobian and IK target is expressed in the group's reference
frame: the work frame when there is one (so a path on the workpiece stays
on it however the positioner turns it), else the root link's frame.
`Manipulator` is the common case: a fixed arm, poses in its base frame.

`q` holds the flange path's DOFs (base first), then the work path's that
the flange path does not share; each is a movable joint driving its own
DOF or the leader of a coupled one. External axes (the work path's
joints, plus any named `externalAxes`) are damped in every solve, so they
move for what the arm cannot do alone; the damping shapes the steps,
never the answer.

A redundant arm has a `swivel` naming its extra motion: given, or for a
7-DOF arm (external axes aside) by default through the pivots of its 2nd,
4th and 6th joints.

One solve entry point, `solve`, takes its settings as `IkOptions`
(tracking or reaching, TCP or flange target, swivel, posture, moving base).
The group itself never changes once built; what an evaluation writes
(the model state, its snapshot, solver scratch) is `KinematicGroupData`.
Each query takes the data to work in, by default this thread's own, so a
group can be shared between threads (a planner and the frame loop).

fields.name: model
fields.doc: The whole robot, compiled.

fields.name: workFrame
fields.doc: Frame poses are expressed in; null for the root link's frame.

fields.name: group
fields.doc: The group DOFs' driving joints and their limits, in `q` order.

fields.name: external
fields.doc: True for each group DOF that is an external axis (damped), in `q` order.

fields.name: swivel
fields.doc: How the swivel (elbow) angle of a redundant arm is measured; null when none is defined.

fields.name: externalWeight
fields.doc: Weight of an external axis's step damping, in the units of the tool task (1 m weighs like 1 rad).

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`externalAxes` names further joints on the flange path to treat as
external (a rail under the arm); the work path's joints always are.

fields.name: jointIndices
fields.doc: The runtime (compiled `RobotModel.joints`) index of each group DOF's driving joint, in `q` order.

fields.name: pathJoints
fields.doc: Every joint from the root link to the flange link (fixed ones included), root first.

fields.name: redundant
fields.doc: True when an arm has more DOFs than a tool pose fixes and a swivel names the extra one.

fields.name: baseMotion
fields.doc:
How the robot's base may move in a solve with `IkOptions.rootPose`:
`Floating` for a `floatingBase` robot, `Planar` (x, y, yaw on the floor)
for a `mobileBase` one, `Fixed` otherwise. Planar treats the base as able
to reach any floor pose, which is right for deciding where to stand, not
for instantaneous motion of a differential drive.

fields.name: threadLocalData
fields.doc:
This thread's working data for the group: what every query uses unless given its own. Kept for
the few groups the thread used last; one evicted and needed again starts afresh, which no
query notices, as each writes the state it reads.

fields.name: newData
fields.doc: Fresh working data for the group, for a caller that keeps its own (a planner, a hot loop).

fields.name: forwardKinematics
fields.doc: The flange's pose in the reference frame.

fields.name: linkPoses
fields.doc:
The poses of the bodies of `links` in the reference frame at joint values `q`, in one evaluation: for placing what
the links carry (collision hulls) as the arm moves.

fields.name: moves
fields.doc: Whether the link moves when one of the group's joints does (it is carried by such a joint, however far out).

fields.name: tcpPose
fields.doc: The tool centre point's pose in the reference frame (the flange composed with `flange_T_tcp`).

fields.name: workPose
fields.doc: The work frame's pose in the root link's frame (the root link's own pose without a work frame).

fields.name: jacobian
fields.doc: Geometric Jacobian at the flange, 6 x n (rows 0..2 linear, 3..5 angular), in the reference frame.

fields.name: pointJacobian
fields.doc:
As `jacobian`, flat row-major, for the point `flangeTPoint` on the
flange (e.g. the TCP): its velocity relative to the reference frame
(which moves with a positioner), expressed in it.

fields.name: tcpJacobian
fields.doc: The Jacobian of the tool centre point: linear rows at the TCP, in the reference frame.

fields.name: swivelAngle
fields.doc:
The swivel angle at `q` in radians (see `ArmSwivel`), or NaN without a
swivel or where it is undefined (the elbow straight, or the
shoulder-wrist line along the reference).

types.name: KinematicGroupData
types.doc:
What evaluating a `KinematicGroup` writes: the model state, its snapshot and the solvers'
scratch. The group stays unchanged, so one group serves any number of threads, each evaluating
in data of its own (`KinematicGroup.threadLocalData`, or `newData` for a caller that keeps it).

fields.name: numericSolves
fields.doc: Numeric pose queries evaluated in this caller-owned or thread-local context.

fields.name: swivelProbe
fields.doc: Measures the swivel of a redundant arm (it keeps scratch of its own); null without one.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Made by `KinematicGroup.newData`, which knows the group's swivel.

types.name: Manipulator
types.doc:
An arm of a robot: the `KinematicGroup` of the joints from `baseLink` to
the link carrying the `flangeFrame`, with its mounted tool (`flangeTTcp`,
identity without one) and no work frame, so poses, Jacobians and IK
targets are in the base link's frame. Everything else (solving,
Jacobians, the swivel of a 7-DOF arm, a moving base) is the group's.

fields.name: withTool
fields.doc: The same arm carrying a different tool; shares the compiled model.

types.name: PayloadCheckResult
types.doc: First load-chart failure along a sampled joint path, or a safe result.

types.name: PayloadChecker
types.doc:
Sample a joint path against a robot's static carried-load chart. Gravity
is in base -Z; acceleration and dynamic joint torques are outside this check.

types.name: ReachLoadBand
types.doc: A load rating valid through the specified flange distance from the base.

types.name: ReachLoadChart
types.doc:
Piecewise robot load chart keyed by 3D flange distance from the base.
More detailed vendor charts can implement RobotLoadChart directly.

types.name: RobotLoadChart
types.doc: Robot-specific static payload envelope. Return null outside its rated domain.

types.name: RobotPayloadLimit
types.doc: Allowed carried mass and gravity moment about the flange at one pose.

types.name: ToolPlanningContext
types.doc: Mounted tool and an authored map-frame collision scene for work planning.

types.name: ForkAxisConfig
types.doc: Named robot joint and permitted target interval for one fork axis.

types.name: ForkAxisState
types.doc: Immutable observed position, velocity, and effort for one fork axis.

types.name: ForkConfig
types.doc: Named fork mechanism joint map and load envelope.

types.name: ForkState
types.doc: Immutable fork observation derived from one RobotSnapshot.

types.name: Forks
types.doc: Named fork mechanism view over a normal Robot instance.

fields.name: fromRobot
fields.doc: Builds the fork view from roles and limits authored on a RobotProfile, resolved against a RobotModel.

fields.name: fromBlueprint
fields.doc: Builds the fork view from a previously compiled robot blueprint.

fields.name: command
fields.doc: Submits all requested axis positions in one heterogeneous-safe joint batch.

types.name: LoadLimits
types.doc: Application-level payload and lift envelope. Native runtime limits remain authoritative.

fields.name: violation
fields.doc: Returns a description when a requested lift state exceeds the configured envelope.

types.name: LoadState
types.doc: Immutable observed load condition; unknown is distinct from a confirmed empty fork.

types.name: Payload
types.doc: Physical payload dimensions and center of mass, expressed in metres and kilograms.

types.name: AckermannDrive
types.doc: Bicycle-model Ackermann steering plus one driven wheel joint.

types.name: DifferentialDrive
types.doc:
Differential-drive wheel velocity mapping. A wheel's direction is +1 when a
positive joint rate rolls it forward and -1 when its joint turns the other
way, such as a right wheel whose axis follows its outward-facing motor shaft;
the compiler derives both from the wheel joints' axes.

types.name: DifferentialOdometry
types.doc: Wheel-position odometry that resets its integration baseline on source-clock changes.

fields.name: leftDirection
fields.doc: +1 when a positive joint rate rolls the wheel forward, -1 when it rolls it back.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Updates and returns odometry from an immutable RobotSnapshot.

types.name: DriveModel
types.doc: Kinematic mapping from a planar body twist to one atomic joint target batch.

fields.name: maxCurvature
fields.doc: Largest feasible magnitude of yaw rate divided by signed body speed.

types.name: Footprint
types.doc: Immutable counter-clockwise polygon describing a robot's planar footprint.

types.name: FootprintPoint
types.doc: Immutable x/y coordinate in a base footprint, measured in metres.

types.name: HolonomicDrive
types.doc:
Omnidirectional ("kiwi") drive: three wheels mounted at 120-degree
intervals around the base center, each rolling tangentially. `targets`
accepts the full `Twist2` body velocity. Navigator/GoTo continue to produce
lateral = 0, while direct callers and work planners can command a strafe.

fields.name: wheelAngles
fields.doc: Mount angle of each wheel about +Z from the base's x axis, in radians.

fields.name: maxCurvature
fields.doc: Every heading is reachable while driving straight, like in-place rotation.

fields.name: createOdometry
fields.doc: No two-wheel differential relationship to decode; HolonomicDrivePlant uses wheelAngles.

types.name: HolonomicOdometry
types.doc:
Wheel-position odometry for a three-wheel omni/kiwi base (see
`HolonomicDrive`). The three wheel angles are 120 degrees apart, so the
inverse of the same tangential speed relationship used by
`HolonomicDrive.targets()` decouples exactly:
`s_i = -sin(theta_i) * distance + cos(theta_i) * lateralDistance +
baseRadius * headingChange`. Forward and lateral displacement are weighted
sums of the wheel distances, while heading change is their average divided
by the base radius.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Updates and returns odometry from an immutable RobotSnapshot.

types.name: MobileBase
types.doc: Configured mobile-drive view over an ordinary Robot instance.

fields.name: fromRobot
fields.doc: Builds the mobile view from roles and dimensions authored on a RobotProfile, resolved against a RobotModel.

fields.name: fromBlueprint
fields.doc: Builds the mobile view from a previously compiled robot blueprint.

fields.name: applySafetyLimits
fields.doc: Applies user-level safety setpoints that can only lower authored limits.

fields.name: applySafetyStop
fields.doc: Blocks MobileBase commands while a user-level policy requires a stop.

fields.name: pathSpeed
fields.doc: Maximum translation speed for a path curvature, including simultaneous wheel motion.

fields.name: command
fields.doc: Limits a body command and submits all drive joints as one RobotCommand.

types.name: MotionLimits
types.doc: Configurable speed and acceleration limits for planar base commands.

fields.name: constrain
fields.doc: Applies speed limits, then acceleration limits when a duration is supplied.

types.name: PlanarMath
types.doc: Small planar helpers missing from the embedded Haxeon Math surface.

types.name: Pose2
types.doc: Immutable planar pose in metres and radians.

fields.name: compose
fields.doc: Applies a pose expressed in this pose's local frame.

fields.name: relativeTo
fields.doc: Returns this pose expressed relative to `origin`.

fields.name: integrate
fields.doc: Integrates a constant body-frame velocity for a positive duration.

fields.name: integrateDisplacement
fields.doc: Integrates body-frame forward/lateral displacement and heading change exactly.

types.name: Pose3
types.doc: Immutable rigid pose in meters with an xyzw quaternion rotation.

fields.name: compose
fields.doc: Composes a local pose into this pose's parent frame.

fields.name: planarPose
fields.doc: Projects the position and local +X heading onto a Z-up planar frame.

fields.name: rotate
fields.doc: Rotates a vector from this pose's local frame into its parent frame.

types.name: Twist2
types.doc: Body-frame planar velocity: +X forward, +Y lateral, and +Z yaw rate.

fields.name: assumed
fields.doc: Assumed engineering inputs carried from the model's source.

fields.name: microsteps
fields.doc: Driver settings and input ceiling, required for stepper actuators.

fields.name: speedLimiter
fields.doc: The bound controller, when its clock further limits the driver.

fields.name: maxEffort
fields.doc: Limits are in the actuator's effort and coordinate units, not joint units.

fields.name: servoStiffness
fields.doc:
Default servo gains in actuator units, such as an MJCF position
actuator's kp and kv: effort per unit of position and velocity error.
Zero means none is authored.

fields.name: positionLoopRate
fields.doc: Position-loop frequency supplied by the driver, Hz; zero when unspecified.

fields.name: drive
fields.doc:
What kind of motor this is and what it can deliver, or null for a bare effort and rate. For a
stepper or a servo, `maxEffort` and `maxRate` are the torque and speed a planner may rely
on (a stepper's usable share of its holding torque, a servo's peak torque and maximum speed),
and the drive carries the rest: the torque-speed curve the plan check compares against.

fields.name: processVelocity
fields.doc: Process velocity binding for a CNC spindle; setpoints come from analog channels, not trajectories.

fields.name: encoder
fields.doc:
The id of the `Encoder` that reads this motor, or empty for none. A servo's feedback comes from it
(the drive also states its feedback resolution).

fields.name: efficiency
fields.doc:
Share of the motor's power its transmission delivers to the joint, such as a gearbox's 0.9; 1 is
lossless. The transmission's ratio is the gearbox ratio: the actuator turns `ratio` times for one turn
of the joint, so the joint gets the motor's torque times the ratio times this, at the motor's speed over
the ratio.

fields.name: fullStepsPerRevolution
fields.doc:
Full steps in one turn of a stepper motor's rotor, 0 when this is not a stepper. A stepper's
actuator coordinate is the rotor angle in radians; microstepping is a property of the driver
wiring, so the deployment adds it. Setting it makes the actuator a stepper known only by its
steps, unless it already is one.

fields.name: planningEffort
fields.doc:
The torque a planner may rely on at any speed. A stepper's `maxEffort` is its usable share of
holding torque; a servo's is its peak torque, and the drive's peak when none is set.

fields.name: planningRate
fields.doc: Missing motor speed stays missing until a stated drive or driver supplies a cap.

fields.name: rateLimiter
fields.doc: The hardware ceiling that is active at the motor's planning rate.

fields.name: torqueCurve
fields.doc: The torque-speed curve the plan check holds this actuator to: its drive's, or flat at its effort and rate.

types.name: ActuatorDrive
types.doc:
What powers an actuator, and what it can deliver. Steppers and servos fail
differently: a stepper that is asked for more torque than its pull-out curve gives loses steps,
a servo that is asked for more than its peak torque falls behind or trips. Drive-level
behaviour only; current loops and thermal mass are left out.

types.name: AxisLoad
types.doc:
What an axis (a joint no other joint leads) asks of its motors: the mass and inertia it moves,
the steady loads on it (gravity, friction) and how stiff and loose its drive is. Built by
`DriveLoads.of`; the plan check turns it into torque along a plan.

fields.name: stiffness
fields.doc: Stiffness of the axis's drive against force on the axis, N/m; 0 when rigid.

fields.name: backlash
fields.doc: Lost motion on reversal at the axis, in its units, summed along the drive.

fields.name: assumed
fields.doc: Assumptions along the axis's motor paths, with duplicates removed.

types.name: Brake
types.doc:
Spring-applied brake on a motor joint. Effort and delays describe the physical device;
release timeout and feedback age describe the controller's admission policy.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (id:String, joint:String, releaseChannel:String, releasedSensor:String, holdingEffort:Float, releaseDelay:Float, applicationDelay:Float, releaseTimeoutMs:Int, feedbackMaxAgeMs:Int):Void

types.name: CollisionApproximation
types.doc: Explicit policy for deriving runtime collision from authored geometry.

types.name: CollisionShape
types.doc: One collision shape, posed in its link's frame.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Source identity, such as a CAD occurrence id.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: Unit quaternion in x, y, z, w order.

fields.name: surface
fields.doc: Contact surface; null keeps the simulator's defaults.

fields.name: convexVertices
fields.doc: Convex vertices in the link frame, including this shape's pose.

fields.name: validate
fields.doc: Returns why the shape is invalid, or null when it is valid.

types.name: ContactPair
types.doc:
An explicit contact between two collision shapes on different links, named
by link ID and index into that link's collisionShapes, with its own surface.
It applies whatever the shapes' own contact modes say.

types.name: ContactSurface
types.doc:
How a collision shape touches others. Zero fields keep the simulator's
default. friction is sliding, torsional and rolling; frictionDimensions is 1
(frictionless), 3 (sliding), 4 (with torsional) or 6 (with rolling);
contactTimeConstant (s) and contactDampingRatio set how stiff and how damped
the soft contact is.

types.name: CylinderDrive
types.doc: Shared double-acting cylinder dimensions, pressure forces and process channels in SI units.

types.name: DriveCompliance
types.doc: Elastic coordinates shared by every driven axis, including rigid motor constraints.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Omitted axes carry zero external force; their elastic coordinates remain free.

types.name: DriveLoads
types.doc:
The axes of a model that actuators drive, through couplings or directly, with what each asks of
them. A joint is an axis when no coupling leads to it as a follower. Joint frames are taken in
a world whose +Z is up; an axis whose direction depends on a turning joint is treated as worst
case for gravity.

types.name: ElasticNetwork
types.doc: Derived span energies; listed motion couplings supply no additional elastic spring.

types.name: ElasticSolve
types.doc: Static span energy with held motors and physical transmission constraints.

types.name: ElasticSpan
types.doc: One free span's axial spring and displacement coordinates, entirely in SI units.

types.name: Encoder
types.doc:
An encoder on a joint: a sensor that reads the joint's position in counts. Which joint it is on
says what it sees. On a motor's own joint it is motor-side: it sees the rotor, so lost steps and a
servo's following error, but not backlash or belt stretch. On a joint the load moves through a
drive it is load-side (a linear scale, or an encoder on the driven pulley): it sees where the load
is, stretch and backlash included. Drive-level only: counts are quantised, with no noise or latency.

The runtime does not compile encoders; a simulation reads them from the joint positions it
reports (see `EncoderReading`), and a device reports its own counts.

fields.name: countsPerUnit
fields.doc: Counts per unit of joint position: per radian on a turning joint, per metre on a sliding one.

fields.name: index
fields.doc:
Whether it has an index pulse: once a revolution on a turning joint, and at the reference mark
(the joint's zero) on a sliding one.

fields.name: perRevolution
fields.doc: An encoder of `counts` per revolution (quadrature counts, so four times the line count) on a turning joint.

fields.name: perMillimetre
fields.doc: A linear scale of `counts` per millimetre on a sliding joint.

fields.name: resolution
fields.doc: The size of one count, in joint units.

fields.name: indexPeriod
fields.doc: Position in joint units between index pulses: a turn, or none for a single reference mark.

types.name: EncoderKind
types.doc: How an encoder reports position: counts since it was powered up, or the position itself.

fields.name: Incremental
fields.doc: Quadrature counts from where the joint was when the encoder was powered up.

fields.name: Absolute
fields.doc: The position itself, in counts from the joint's zero.

types.name: EncoderReading
types.doc:
What an encoder reports at one moment: its count, and how many index pulses it has passed since it
was powered up. `power` is the joint position it was powered up at, which an incremental encoder
counts from; an absolute one counts from the joint's zero.

fields.name: power
fields.doc: Joint position the encoder was powered up at, in joint units.

fields.name: sample
fields.doc: Reads the encoder with its joint at `position`: the count is quantised to whole counts.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: The joint position this count stands for, the reading as the machine would use it.

types.name: Frame
types.doc: Editable link_T_frame mount, in meters and unit xyzw quaternion.

fields.name: flangeIncludePath
fields.doc: Owning include when this is a standard robot flange; null for other frames.

types.name: FrameId
types.doc: Persistent semantic frame identity, never a runtime array index.

types.name: HydraulicDrive
types.doc: Flow-limited hydraulic cylinder. Coincident coil states close the valve centre.

types.name: HydraulicDriveRecord
types.doc: Current RobotModel hydraulic drive payload, in metres, seconds, Pa and N.

fields.name: includePath
fields.doc: Assembly include that owns this joint; null for non-assembly models.

fields.name: passive
fields.doc: No position command or power-on hold; gravity, contact and constraints own its motion.

fields.name: mechanicalLimits
fields.doc: Mechanical inputs retained when `limits` becomes the compiled effective result.

fields.name: armature
fields.doc: Reflected rotor inertia: kg m^2, or kg for a prismatic joint.

fields.name: damping
fields.doc: Viscous effort per unit joint velocity.

fields.name: frictionLoss
fields.doc: Dry friction effort.

fields.name: limitTimeConstant
fields.doc:
How soft the joint's limits are, like a soft contact: time constant (s)
and damping ratio, and MuJoCo's five-term impedance curve. Zeros keep the
simulator's default.

types.name: JointCoupling
types.doc:
One term of a follower joint's coordinate, in SI units: the follower is the sum of its couplings,
`Σ (ratio * leader + offset)`. Most followers have one coupling (a lead screw follows its axis); a
follower with several, such as a CoreXY motor that follows both axes, has one coupling per leader,
each with its own efficiency, stiffness, backlash and drag. A leader appears once per follower, and
the couplings never form a cycle (see `cycleThrough`).

types.name: JointId
types.doc: Stable joint identity within a robot model; never a runtime index.

fields.name: velocityLimiter
fields.doc: The hardware ceiling, when it supplies the effective velocity cap.

fields.name: overtravel
fields.doc:
How far the joint can travel past `lower` and `upper` before it meets its
end stop, in joint units, as a machine's limit switch sits beyond its soft
limit. Commands stay within the limits; the runtime faults only past this.

fields.name: rackingTolerance
fields.doc: Permitted dual-drive disagreement in SI joint units; zero means unstated.

fields.name: requireVelocity
fields.doc: Require a stated or derived cap when a planner needs a finite limit. Zero remains a valid cap.

types.name: JointSwitch
types.doc: A physical home or limit switch, expressed in the monitored joint's SI coordinate.

fields.name: side
fields.doc: -1 trips toward decreasing coordinates, +1 toward increasing coordinates.

fields.name: repeatability
fields.doc: Bounded closing-position variation, rather than noise on every tick.

fields.name: driveJoint
fields.doc: Optional motor follower sensed by this physical side, rather than the shared leader.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (id:String, joint:JointId, frameId:FrameId, role:String, side:Int, trip:Float, hysteresis:Float, repeatability:Float, ?seed:Int, ?driveJoint:JointId, ?homeAfter:Array<String>):Void

types.name: LinkId
types.doc: Stable link identity within a robot model; never a runtime index.

types.name: MotorLoad
types.doc: One motor's place in the drive of an axis: how the axis's motion and force reach its rotor.

fields.name: joint
fields.doc: The joint the motor's transmission drives.

fields.name: ratio
fields.doc: Motor coordinate (rotor radians for a stepper or servo) per unit of the axis, signed.

fields.name: efficiency
fields.doc: Share of power the couplings between the axis and the motor pass on.

types.name: PneumaticDrive
types.doc: Pressure effort with a spring-return or latched directional valve.

types.name: ProcessVelocityDrive
types.doc: Analog process channels selecting a signed velocity for one continuous joint.

fields.name: radiansPerSpeedUnit
fields.doc: Radians per second for one unit of the speed channel.

types.name: QuantityAssumption
types.doc: An assumption names the quantity it affects, so findings report only relevant inputs.

types.name: RobotDefinition
types.doc: A mechanical model and its separately authored interpretation, passed together by consumers.

types.name: RobotModel
types.doc: Editable static definition of a robot's links, joints, and sensors.

fields.name: actuators
fields.doc: Multiple actuators may address one joint through independent transmissions.

fields.name: couplings
fields.doc: Mechanical joint-to-joint relations, independent of actuator transmissions.

fields.name: elasticNetworks
fields.doc: Physical elastic networks, independent of the nominal motion equations.

fields.name: encoders
fields.doc: Encoders on joints; they are read from joint positions rather than compiled into the runtime.

fields.name: switches
fields.doc: Physical switch thresholds; readings are supplied as external digital sensors.

fields.name: contactPairs
fields.doc: Explicit contacts between link collision shapes.

fields.name: floatingBase
fields.doc:
True when the root link is a free six-DOF body, as for a legged or
humanoid robot, rather than a base fixed to the world. This replaces a
floating joint: runtime joints stay one-DOF.

fields.name: encoderFor
fields.doc: The sensor explicitly wired as this actuator's feedback.

fields.name: followsSpring
fields.doc: Whether joint `id` is the follower of a spring coupling (`JointCoupling.isSpring`): a belt stretches from it.

fields.name: coupledLimits
fields.doc:
Joint `id`'s limits, tightened by every joint that moves with it through couplings and by
the actuators that drive them, in `id`'s units. A lead screw's speed limit caps the axis it
turns with; a motor caps it at its rate through the ratios. For a sliding joint driven by
actuators, acceleration is also capped at their summed force, through each coupling's
efficiency, over the mass the joint carries plus every coupled joint's turning inertia (rotor
armature included) seen through the ratio. Gravity and friction are left out. A missing limit is null; zero is a stopped joint. With `steady` loads, the force left for acceleration is what the motors give
less their drag, the axis's rail friction and its weight (see `SteadyLoads`).

A follower that sums several leaders (a CoreXY motor) binds each leader inside a box: the axis's
speed is limited to the follower's limit over the sum of the ratios' magnitudes (through chains,
`couplingWeight`), so every combination of moves within the per-axis limits stays inside it.
`motorSpaceVelocity` returns the single-axis velocity envelope instead: callers must enforce the
coupled motor velocity sums in their planner and retain follower limits in the runtime.
Each axis likewise gets only its share of such a motor's force, in proportion to its ratio.

fields.name: materializeLimits
fields.doc: Materialise all drive caps from one snapshot, then fill missing follower caps from their leaders.

fields.name: turningInertia
fields.doc:
What accelerating `joint` moves, in its own units: for a revolute joint the moment of inertia of everything it
carries about its axis (kg m^2), for a prismatic joint the carried mass (kg); armature included.

fields.name: validate
fields.doc:
Performs the lightweight model checks used by editors.

Runtime creation must use `RobotRuntimeCompiler.validate(model, profile)` or `compile()`;
that pass also checks backend support and graph topology and returns
structured diagnostics.

types.name: RobotModelCodec
types.doc: Canonical, versioned JSON artifact for an editable RobotModel.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: Null mounts at the root link origin; otherwise references a model frame.

fields.name: zoneBoxes
fields.doc: A `zone_input`'s boxes in its frame: six numbers per box, its centre and half extents, in metres.

fields.name: joint
fields.doc: Joint read by a native switch or speed sensor.

fields.name: windowLower
fields.doc: Switch position window in SI units; for `at_speed`, lower is fractional speed tolerance.

fields.name: hysteresis
fields.doc: Switch position hysteresis in SI units; for `at_speed`, fractional speed hysteresis.

fields.name: startAngleRadians
fields.doc: Bearing of the first LiDAR ray in the sensor frame.

fields.name: fieldOfViewRadians
fields.doc: Angular coverage. The default is one full revolution.

fields.name: validZoneBoxes
fields.doc: Whether `boxes` holds one or more boxes of a finite centre and three positive half extents.

types.name: SensorId
types.doc: Stable sensor identity within a robot model; never a runtime index.

types.name: ServoDrive
types.doc:
A servo: rated (continuous) and peak torque, rated and maximum speed, rotor inertia, encoder
counts per revolution and its torque-speed envelope. Its gains, when authored, are the
actuator's `servoStiffness` and `servoDamping`.

types.name: ShapeContact
types.doc: Which contacts a collision shape takes part in.

fields.name: Layers
fields.doc: Collides like the rest of the robot: with the environment and, unless disabled, other links.

fields.name: PairsOnly
fields.doc: Collides only through the robot's contact pairs.

fields.name: PairsAndEnvironment
fields.doc: Collides through contact pairs and with every environment object, using its own surface.

types.name: SteadyLoads
types.doc:
The loads on a machine that do not depend on its motion, which a drive must carry on top of
accelerating: gravity and friction. They are assumptions, not datasheet values.

fields.name: railDrag
fields.doc:
Running friction of a sliding axis's rails, in N, for an axis whose joint carries no friction of
its own (`Joint.frictionLoss`). Assumption: about 5 N for a hobby-class axis on preloaded
recirculating-ball rail blocks. Rail makers quote friction coefficients of roughly 0.002 to
0.005 of the preload plus seal drag; no value for any particular block is used.

types.name: StepperDrive
types.doc:
A stepper: full steps in one turn, holding torque and a pull-out curve of the torque it keeps
while stepping at each speed. Microstepping is a property of the driver wiring, so the
deployment adds it.

types.name: SwitchReading
types.doc: Deterministic mechanical switch state with a distinct release threshold.

fields.name: edgePosition
fields.doc: Exact mechanical edge coordinate; null until an edge is observed.

fields.name: closingEdgePosition
fields.doc: Latest closing edge, retained separately from the release edge.

fields.name: sample
fields.doc: Samples actual position, including mechanical slip, in the joint's SI units.

types.name: TorqueSpeedCurve
types.doc:
Torque a drive can deliver at each speed, as points joined by straight lines: speeds in
ascending order (in the drive's coordinate units per second, rad/s for a rotor) and the torque
at each (N m). Below the first speed the first torque holds; above the last speed the drive can
deliver nothing. Both stepper pull-out curves and servo torque-speed envelopes use it.

fields.name: flat
fields.doc: The same torque up to `maxSpeed`, then nothing: how a drive with only two numbers behaves.

fields.name: torqueAt
fields.doc: Torque available at `speed`, in either direction.

fields.name: peakTorque
fields.doc: The most torque at any speed.

fields.name: maxSpeed
fields.doc: The highest speed with any torque.

fields.name: flatten
fields.doc: Alternating speed, torque, for saving.

fields.name: scaledSpeeds
fields.doc: A copy with every speed multiplied by `factor`, for a change of the coordinate's units.

types.name: Transmission
types.doc:
Kinematic conversion from an actuator coordinate to a joint coordinate.
SimpleTransmission uses SI units: joint = offset + actuator / ratio.
A rotary actuator driving a prismatic joint therefore has ratio in rad/m;
a rotary-to-rotary ratio is dimensionless.

types.name: UrdfImport
types.doc: A loaded URDF robot and what the loader could not carry over.

fields.name: warnings
fields.doc: Human-readable notes on elements that were skipped or approximated.

types.name: UrdfLoader
types.doc:
Loads an expanded URDF document into a RobotModel (robotkit/plans/HUMANOID.md,
HU-D2). `xacro` must be expanded beforehand.

URDF places each joint frame at its child link's origin: `origin` is the
child frame in the parent, `axis` is in the joint (child) frame, and inertia
is given in the `inertial` frame. A root link named `world` is dropped: a
floating joint from it sets `floatingBase`, a fixed one leaves the robot
fixed. Box, cylinder and sphere collision geometry becomes collision shapes;
mesh references are kept as geometry references. `dynamics` damping and
friction become joint damping and friction loss, `mimic` a joint coupling,
and a simple `transmission` an actuator.

fields.name: PLACEHOLDER_MASS
fields.doc: Mass given to a link without an `inertial`, which the runtime requires to be positive.

types.name: AStarPlanner
types.doc:
Deterministic 8-connected A* over a Costmap2.

The robot is wherever it is, so the start cell is always accepted. A start
inside a blocked but not lethal cell (the costmap's discretization margin,
where the robot can stand without touching anything) plans an escape: the
route may pass through further blocked, non-lethal cells, at a penalty, only
until it first reaches a traversable cell, and never re-enters blocked cells
after that. A start in a traversable cell plans exactly as if escapes did not
exist.

types.name: Costmap2
types.doc:
Traversability and inflation costs over an OccupancyGrid2. Occupied cells,
dynamic obstacle disks, and (by default) unknown cells are inflated by the
robot radius. A soft cost falls off beyond the inflated boundary.

A cell is lethal when a robot centred on it would overlap an obstacle, and
blocked (not traversable) when it is lethal or within half a cell diagonal
of that: the extra margin keeps a route through cell centres clear wherever
in the cell the robot actually is. A robot can therefore stand in a blocked
cell without touching anything, and a planner may escape from one through
cells that are not lethal.

fields.name: obstacleMemorySeconds
fields.doc:
How long (s) an obstacle sensed once stays in the dynamic layer after it was last seen, unless a later
observation sees through its place; zero keeps only what the latest observation shows.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: Counts the changes to the costs, so a view of them can tell when to redraw.

fields.name: refresh
fields.doc: Rebuilds cached costs after the underlying occupancy grid changes.

fields.name: setDynamicObstacles
fields.doc:
Replaces the dynamic obstacle layer and refreshes costs. An unchanged set (a sensor that has not
scanned since) costs nothing; a changed one redraws only the disks, not the grid.

fields.name: senseObstacles
fields.doc:
Takes one observation's obstacles into the dynamic layer, `elapsedSeconds` after the last. With a memory,
an obstacle that is no longer seen stays until the memory runs out, unless `view` shows free space where
it stood; one seen again (overlapping its disk) is replaced by the new sighting. Time is the sum of
the elapsed durations, so it follows the caller's (simulation) clock.

fields.name: dynamicLayer
fields.doc: The dynamic obstacles now in the layer.

fields.name: isLethal
fields.doc: True when a robot centred on the cell would overlap an obstacle, or off the grid.

fields.name: cellCost
fields.doc: Returns nonnegative traversal cost, or a large sentinel if blocked.

types.name: FloorBox
types.doc: A posed obstacle box, with dimensions in metres and yaw in radians.

types.name: FloorMap
types.doc: Rasterizes posed obstacle boxes for both navigation execution and upstream parking planners.

fields.name: navigationMargin
fields.doc: Leave space to detour around inflated obstacles even when only the selected goals bound the map.

types.name: GridCell2
types.doc: Integer address of one cell in an OccupancyGrid2.

types.name: MotionGuard
types.doc:
Software collision-avoidance filter for a path follower. Perception obstacles
must be in the localization body or reference frame; other frames stop motion
until a frame-aware perception stage transforms them. Moving forward or back,
the base slows and stops for what lies in its corridor; a base that is only
turning, or held short of an obstacle but asked to turn, is held only by an
obstacle within reach of its footprint's turning circle, so it can turn away
from one it stopped short of.

fields.name: costmap
fields.doc:
The costmap whose dynamic layer the guard judges instead of the latest observation, so it holds for
what the costmap remembers (an obstacle behind it, or between two rays) and keeps no memory of its own.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Updates the obstacle set and advances one navigation control iteration.

fields.name: updateObservation
fields.doc: Updates localization and obstacle data from the same robot observation.

fields.name: updatePerception
fields.doc: Replaces guard observations without advancing Navigation.

fields.name: detach
fields.doc: Removes this guard's command filter.

types.name: MotionGuardState
types.doc: Current software obstacle response; this is not a safety-rated state.

types.name: Navigation
types.doc: Application-frequency pure-pursuit path follower over localization and MobileBase.

fields.name: lookaheadTime
fields.doc: Additional lookahead seconds; distance grows with the recent commanded speed.

fields.name: rotateToHeadingAngle
fields.doc:
Driving forward, a drive that can turn in place does so first when the route's lookahead point
lies more than this far off its heading, in radians, instead of sweeping a wide arc: leaving a
goal that faces a wall, an arc would run into it. Infinity always follows the arc.

fields.name: crossTrackError
fields.doc: Signed cross-track error, positive to the left of the path direction.

fields.name: follow
fields.doc:
Starts following a framed polyline; the final waypoint supplies the
default goal. Use startDistance to resume on a path after its first pose.

fields.name: followTrajectory
fields.doc: Starts tracking a time-parameterized trajectory with pose feedback.

fields.name: updateObservation
fields.doc: Consumes one robot observation, updates localization, and advances the controller.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Runs one control iteration using the localization service's latest state.

fields.name: setCommandFilter
fields.doc: Installs a final command filter used by operational motion guards.

fields.name: hasCommandFilter
fields.doc: Whether a command filter is currently owned by an operational layer.

types.name: NavigationGoal
types.doc: Framed target pose and arrival tolerances for path following.

types.name: NavigationStatus
types.doc: Lifecycle state for one Navigation path-following request.

types.name: Navigator
types.doc:
Goal-level layer over a Planner and Navigation path follower. It refreshes
dynamic obstacles, replans when the remaining path becomes blocked, and
retries blocked goals after the map has had time to change.

fields.name: replanCount
fields.doc: Number of replanning attempts after the initial plan.

fields.name: navigateTo
fields.doc: Plans from current localization and starts following the requested goal.

fields.name: update
fields.doc:
Updates dynamic obstacles and advances goal execution. Perception obstacles
must already be expressed in the costmap frame.

fields.name: cancel
fields.doc: Stops execution and discards the active goal.

types.name: NavigatorStatus
types.doc: Lifecycle state for goal planning and path following.

types.name: OccupancyCell
types.doc: Discrete occupancy values stored by an OccupancyGrid2.

types.name: OccupancyGrid2
types.doc:
Mutable planar occupancy grid. `origin` is the pose of the lower-left grid
corner in `frameId`; cell coordinates address areas of `resolution` metres.

fields.name: worldToCell
fields.doc: Converts a frame pose to a cell, returning null when outside the grid.

fields.name: occupiedWithin
fields.doc: True when an occupied cell lies within `radiusMeters` of the point (cell centres, so a cell's own extent counts).

fields.name: cellCenter
fields.doc: Returns the center pose of a grid cell in `frameId`.

types.name: Path
types.doc: Immutable polyline of planar poses expressed in one named frame.

fields.name: distanceAtWaypoint
fields.doc: Returns the accumulated arc length at one authored waypoint.

fields.name: poseAt
fields.doc: Returns the path pose at an arc-length distance from its start.

fields.name: project
fields.doc:
Projects onto a bounded, not-yet-traversed portion of the path. Progress
never moves backwards; callers can also cap forward progress to avoid
jumping onto a later branch at a crossing or loop.

fields.name: nearestDistance
fields.doc: Compatibility helper returning only the projected arc length.

types.name: PathProjection
types.doc: Closest point on a path segment, with signed left-positive cross-track error.

types.name: PathSpeedLimit
types.doc: Maximum body speed allowed over one arc-length interval of a Path.

types.name: Planner
types.doc: Plans a traversable path between poses expressed in the planner's map frame.

fields.name: plan
fields.doc: Throws when either pose is outside the map, blocked, or unreachable.

types.name: Trajectory
types.doc: Immutable time-parameterized planar path.

fields.name: fromPath
fields.doc:

types.name: PlaneFit
types.doc:
Least-squares plane fitting (total least squares via the 3x3 point
covariance and `JacobiEigenSolver`) plus seeded RANSAC for outlier

fields.name: fit
fields.doc:
Fits `normal . x = offset` by minimizing the sum of squared orthogonal
distances: the normal is the covariance matrix's smallest-eigenvalue
eigenvector, and the offset is `normal . centroid`. `referenceNormal`,
when given, orients the (otherwise sign-ambiguous) normal onto the same
side.

fields.name: fitRansac
fields.doc:
Seeded RANSAC: repeatedly samples three points to build a candidate
plane, keeps the candidate with the most inliers within
`inlierThreshold`, then refits (`fit`) over just that consensus set for
the final estimate. Deterministic for a fixed `seed`.

determinism rule).

types.name: GravityEstimator
types.doc:
The direction of gravity in the base frame, estimated from a gyroscope and
an accelerometer alone, as a robot's own controller has to: it has no
simulator to ask.

The estimate is the unit vector d that points down. The gyroscope rotates
it, d' = -w x d, which drifts; the accelerometer measures specific force f,
which at rest is -g, so -f/|f| points down and pulls the estimate back with a
complementary-filter gain. Only while the robot is still does it pull: when
|f| differs from gravity, or the body turns, the pull fades out. Walking
accelerates the body in step with its bobbing, and an accelerometer averaged
over a gait reads a gravity tilted by 0.05 to 0.1 rad, which the policy
would then lean against. Feed it at the IMU's rate, not the control rate.
This is the projected-gravity vector that legged-locomotion policies take,
(0, 0, -1) when upright.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`gain` is the accelerometer's pull in 1/s when the robot is still (the
filter's time constant is its inverse); `trust` is the fraction of gravity
by which |f| may differ, and `stillRate` the angular rate (rad/s) at which
the body counts as moving, before the pull fades out entirely.

types.name: OnnxPolicy
types.doc:
A learned policy: an ONNX model run on the CPU by ONNX Runtime. It is a
pure function from named float tensors to named float tensors; state a
controller must carry between calls (a recurrent network's, say) is an
ordinary input the caller feeds back from an output.

fields.name: load
fields.doc: Loads a model file. Throws when it cannot be read or uses unsupported tensors.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: The input tensor called `name`; throws for an unknown name.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: The output tensor called `name`; throws for an unknown name.

fields.name: run
fields.doc:
Runs the model once. Every input must be given, with exactly its element
count; outputs come back by name.

types.name: PolicyController
types.doc:
Runs a learned policy as a joint controller: each control period it reads
encoders and the base IMU, builds the policy's observation, evaluates the
network and returns joint servo targets (JointTarget.servo: the joint's
`kp (q_target - q) - kd qdot` evaluated every physics step, HU-D3).

The controller sees what a real robot's controller would (HU-D4): encoder
positions and velocities, the IMU's gyroscope and accelerometer, its own last
action and the velocity command. The direction of gravity comes from a
complementary filter on the IMU, not from the simulator. Until the first IMU
sample arrives the controller holds the default pose.

fields.name: evaluations
fields.doc: Policy evaluations so far; the gait clock is this times the control period.

fields.name: clampedTargets
fields.doc: Policy targets that had to be clamped into a joint's travel so far.

fields.name: debugTruth
fields.doc: Enables the privileged state debugging tools compare the estimator to; never set it in a real controller.

fields.name: prepareModel
fields.doc:
Adds the spec's IMU to `model` when it has no sensor of that ID, mounted
on the spec's link. Call before compiling the model.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Forgets the network's state, the history, the IMU filter and the gait clock.

fields.name: ready
fields.doc: True once an IMU sample has been seen and the policy is driving the joints.

fields.name: estimatedDown
fields.doc: The estimator's current down vector in the base frame.

fields.name: standTargets
fields.doc: Servo targets that hold every joint at the default (and hold) pose.

fields.name: update
fields.doc:
Evaluates the policy once. `q` and `dq` are the robot's joint positions and
velocities in model order and `sensors` its latest sensor frames.

fields.name: observeImu
fields.doc:
Feeds the IMU's latest sample to the gravity filter. Call it on every
sensor update, which may be much faster than the control period: the
filter integrates the gyroscope between policy evaluations, and sampling it
only once per evaluation aliases the gait's impacts into a tilt bias.

types.name: PolicySession
types.doc:
The execution session of a policy-driven robot. It closes the loop every
control period: read the robot, sample the velocity reference, evaluate the
policy and submit its joint servo targets, all through the `Robot` boundary,
so the same session drives a simulated, remote or replayed robot and a
RecordingRobot records what it sends.

The velocity command is a cyclic reference (VelocityReference, LD-D3): it
carries a sequence and a deadline, and when it lapses the reference brakes to
zero. Zero is "hold": the policy keeps balancing in place, joints are never
frozen.

Call `start()` once, then `update()` after each simulation (or device) step.

fields.name: lastCommand
fields.doc: The velocity the policy was last given.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`tickSeconds` is the period at which `update()` is called: the simulation
tick, or the device's sensor period. The IMU is read on every tick and the
policy runs every `controlPeriod / tickSeconds` ticks, which must be a
whole number; the default is one evaluation per tick.

fields.name: start
fields.doc:
Holds the default pose from the first physics step. For `warmupSeconds`
the policy stays off while the robot settles and the IMU filter finds down,
as a real robot's would while it stands before the walking controller is
enabled.

fields.name: command
fields.doc:
Submits a velocity command valid until `deadlineNs` on the robot's clock;
sequences must increase, and this session numbers them itself.

fields.name: commandFor
fields.doc: Commands `velocity` for `seconds` from the robot's present time.

fields.name: update
fields.doc:
One tick: read the robot and feed its IMU to the gravity filter, and once
per control period sample the reference, evaluate the policy and command.
Returns the targets it sent, empty between evaluations.

types.name: PolicySpec
types.doc:
Everything a controller needs to run a learned policy on a robot, apart from
the network itself: what the network sees and how its output becomes joint
servo targets. It is authored beside the model as JSON (`policy.json`).

Observation terms are scaled element-wise, as in training; a scale is one
number or one per element.

fields.doc: Free-form provenance: where the policy came from and under which licence.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: ONNX file, relative to the spec file.

fields.name: controlPeriod
fields.doc: Seconds between policy evaluations.

fields.name: historyLength
fields.doc: Observations stacked into the input, newest last; 1 means no history.

fields.name: joints
fields.doc: RobotModel joint IDs the policy drives, in the order of its observation and action.

fields.name: actionScale
fields.doc: target = default + actionScale * action.

types.name: VelocityCommand
types.doc: A planar velocity command: forward, lateral (m/s) and yaw rate (rad/s), in the robot's base frame.

types.name: VelocityReference
types.doc:
The velocity command a walking controller follows, as a cyclic reference
(motionkit/plans/LANE_D_REDUNDANCY_SERVO.md, LD-D3) rather than a queue of
trajectories to replace:

- every command carries a sequence, and a deadline on the clock the
controller runs on; older or equal sequences are rejected;
- the target is clamped to the configured limits;
- the value the controller reads changes no faster than the acceleration
limits, so a step in the command is a ramp; and
- when the deadline passes without a newer command the target becomes zero,
and the value brakes to a stop within the same limits, so a lost
controller leaves the robot standing, not walking on.

fields.name: expired
fields.doc: Whether the last accepted command's deadline has passed.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`limit` and `acceleration` are per axis (forward, lateral, yaw): the
largest magnitude of the command and the fastest it may change per second.

fields.name: submit
fields.doc:
Accepts a command, or names why not. `deadlineNs` is on the same clock as
`sample`'s `nowNs`, which the caller must pass (a zero deadline is already
past).

fields.name: clear
fields.doc: Drops the command at once: the target is zero from the next sample.

fields.name: sample
fields.doc: Advances the reference to `nowNs` and returns the velocity to follow.

fields.name: targetCommand
fields.doc: The clamped target the reference is heading for, zero once expired.

types.name: DifferentialDrivePlant
types.doc:
Ideal rolling-kinematics plant for a differential-drive robot in SimKit.

Couples the robot's wheel joints to its kinematic base through the native
simulation: every tick, after the robot applies its commands and before
physics advances, the base rolls by the wheel velocity targets the robot
actually applied for that tick. Those are the runtime's rate-clamped targets
whether they came from MobileBase or were submitted straight to the robot,
and they are zero after a normal or emergency stop or a safety reset, so the
chassis follows every stop on the tick it takes effect with no added
latency. Articulated joints and sensors still advance through the shared
simulation, and the IMU measures the chassis motion.

fields.name: pose
fields.doc:
Planar base pose after the latest step or teleport: position on the floor
and heading (unwrapped). The base keeps its authored roll and pitch.

fields.name: baseHeight
fields.doc: Base height, preserved while the plant drives the planar pose.

fields.name: teleport
fields.doc:
Jumps the chassis for the next tick while keeping wheel targets, sensor
history, and the chassis velocity; the jump itself does not read as motion.
The chassis keeps its height and its roll and pitch relative to its
heading, as the native plant does while it drives.

types.name: EncoderFindingKind
types.doc: What an encoder says is wrong: a motor that is not where it was told to be.

fields.name: LostSteps
fields.doc: A stepper's encoder is further from the commanded position than its bound: the motor lost steps.

fields.name: FollowingError
fields.doc: A servo's (or any other motor's) encoder is further from the command than its bound.

types.name: EncoderMonitor
types.doc:
Reads a robot's encoders from its measured joint positions and compares them with where the joints were
commanded to be. Monitoring only: it names what it finds and never commands anything.

- A **motor-side** encoder (one on a joint a motor drives directly) sees the rotor, so it sees what
the command hides: a stepper's lost steps, a servo's following error. Past `bound` it latches a
finding, `LostSteps` for a stepper and `FollowingError` otherwise. It does not see backlash or
belt stretch, which sit between the rotor and the load.
- A **load-side** encoder (a linear scale, an encoder on a driven pulley) sees where the load is, so
its error against the command is the **path error** the machine really has, the observed
counterpart of the plan check's accuracy prediction (`pathError`). It faults nothing.

`bounds` gives a joint's bound in joint units (the runtime blueprint's `following_error_bound`);
where it has none or zero, a stepper's is `STEPPER_BOUND_STEPS` full steps of its rotor and anything
else's is `DEFAULT_BOUND_COUNTS` encoder counts, both assumptions. A device that counts edges in
hardware feeds `EncoderReading` its own counts and calls `evaluate`.

fields.name: STEPPER_BOUND_STEPS
fields.doc: A stepper may be this many full steps from its command before it is called lost.

fields.name: DEFAULT_BOUND_COUNTS
fields.doc: Counts a non-stepper motor may be from its command.

fields.name: findings
fields.doc: Findings in the order they were made, one per encoder.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `positions` are the joints' positions the encoders power up at; `bounds` maps joint ids to bounds in joint units.

fields.name: motorSide
fields.doc: Whether the encoder is on a joint a motor drives (motor-side) rather than a load joint.

fields.name: observe
fields.doc: Reads every encoder from the measured joint positions and checks it against the commanded ones.

fields.name: evaluate
fields.doc: Checks the readings as they are, such as counts a device reported, against the commanded joint positions.

fields.name: faults
fields.doc: Whether any motor-side encoder has faulted.

fields.name: pathError
fields.doc: The path error a load-side (or any) encoder has measured so far: its latest, worst and RMS error against the command, in joint units.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Forgets what was measured and the faults, and powers the encoders up again at `positions`, as a homing does.

types.doc: The deployment actuator that drives an extruder, and which way its step count goes when it pushes filament in.

fields.name: feed
fields.doc: +1 when the actuator's steps count up as filament is pushed in, -1 when they count down (a motor geared the other way round).

fields.name: onChannel

types.name: HeaterSetup

fields.name: targetChannel
fields.doc: The analog channel the target (degrees Celsius) is set on, and the fan channel that blows on this heater, if any.

fields.name: extruder
fields.doc: The extruder this heater feeds (pushing filament while cold is a fault), or null.

fields.name: minExtrusionTemperature
fields.doc: The material's minimum extrusion temperature; 0 leaves cold extrusion unchecked.

fields.name: tuning
fields.doc: The thermistor, controller and plant, as the caller stated them.

types.name: HeaterTuning
types.doc:
Everything a heater's board and thermal plant are told, none of it defaulted: the thermistor and its front end, the PID
and its band and watchdog, and the plant (its heat capacity, power, loss to the room and the fan's). The caller states
every one, from the part or the job, so a heater cannot run on numbers nobody chose.

types.name: HolonomicDrivePlant
types.doc:
Ideal rolling-kinematics plant for an omnidirectional-base robot in
SimKit, the three-omni-wheel counterpart of `DifferentialDrivePlant`.

Couples the robot's wheel joints to its kinematic base through the native
simulation: every tick, after the robot applies its commands and before
physics advances, the base moves by the full planar body twist (forward,
lateral, and yaw rate) decoded from the wheel velocity targets the robot
actually applied for that tick. Those are the runtime's rate-clamped
targets whether they came from MobileBase or were submitted straight to the
robot, and they are zero after a normal or emergency stop or a safety
reset, so the chassis follows every stop with no added latency, and wheels
driven directly can strafe through the full `Twist2` command.

fields.name: pose
fields.doc:
Planar base pose after the latest step or teleport: position on the floor
and heading (unwrapped). The base keeps its authored roll and pitch.

fields.name: baseHeight
fields.doc: Base height, preserved while the plant drives the planar pose.

fields.name: teleport
fields.doc:
Jumps the chassis for the next tick while keeping wheel targets, sensor
history, and the chassis velocity; the jump itself does not read as motion.
The chassis keeps its height and its roll and pitch relative to its
heading, as the native plant does while it drives.
