types.name: RobotRuntime
types.doc:
Per-robot realtime execution boundary.

A `RobotRuntime` owns one command mailbox and one immutable state stream.
Standalone runtimes own a worker lifecycle; runtimes created by a
`Simulation` are externally driven and advance only through that shared
simulation so all robots observe one physics tick.

fields.name: sourceClockId
fields.doc: Current identity of the endpoint timeline, including its reset epoch.

fields.name: couplings
fields.doc: The blueprint's joint couplings: a joint a plan leaves out follows its leader.

fields.name: contacts
fields.doc: Contacts from the latest simulation tick. Standalone runtimes have none.

fields.name: toolProximity
fields.doc: Inactive proximity contacts on attached tool pieces.

fields.name: create
fields.doc: Creates a runtime from a compiled model and an endpoint factory's result.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Starts a standalone runtime worker; Simulation-owned runtimes reject this.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: Stops a standalone worker; it never advances a shared Simulation.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: Reads the endpoint's supported modes and bounded plan contracts.

fields.name: submitTargets
fields.doc:
Submits a complete heterogeneous joint-target batch in one native call.
`expiresAtNs` (robot source clock, as in snapshots) makes the batch's
velocity targets lapse then: the runtime brakes those joints to zero.

fields.name: submitPlan
fields.doc:
Accepts a plan atomically, including its revision and horizon checks. A
plan carrying native segment arrays reaches the runtime in place and is
copied once there; managed segments are flattened into arrays first. Only
the small header is marshalled field by field, into storage reused across
plans.

fields.name: pollEvents
fields.doc: Drains output changes produced by the runtime owner clock.

fields.name: channelValue
fields.doc:
A process channel's current output value, as the device on it sees it, without draining the
events `pollEvents` reports.

fields.name: writeOutput
fields.doc: Writes a declared digital or analog process output from controller logic.

fields.name: submitPositions
fields.doc: Submits all position targets in one native call.

fields.name: submitPosition
fields.doc: Submits one position target without implying ownership of a simulation tick.

fields.name: submitStop
fields.doc: Submits a stop to the owner thread; it never steps synchronously.

fields.name: submitHold
fields.doc: Pauses, resumes, or aborts a native execution path.

fields.name: resetSafety
fields.doc: Clears a latched safety stop only after the application has acknowledged it.

fields.name: latchHome
fields.doc: Latch an actual home edge in endpoint/counter coordinates, never an ordinary move.

fields.name: calibrateHomeDrives
fields.doc: Apply fresh side latches as one atomic endpoint counter-origin transaction.

fields.name: tryCalibrateHomeDrives
fields.doc: Return false while an identical device batch awaits acknowledgment/fresh state.

fields.name: homeDriveOffset
fields.doc: Read the individual motor-side zero captured by a physical home switch.

fields.name: referenceOffset
fields.doc: Coordinate translation used to convert endpoint edge captures after latch.

fields.name: physicalPositions
fields.doc: Actual endpoint coordinates for physical switch synthesis, unaffected by coordinate zeros.

fields.name: copyPhysicalPositionsInto
fields.doc: Copies actual endpoint coordinates into caller-owned storage for per-tick observers.

fields.name: installSensorPoller
fields.doc: Install a device sensor source before exposing the runtime to consumers.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Reads connection/safety status without materializing joint or sensor snapshots.

fields.name: jointObservation
fields.doc: Joint counter sample for observers that do not consume sensor or execution state.

fields.name: copyJointObservationInto
fields.doc: Copies joint counters into caller-owned storage and returns their source timestamp.

fields.name: copyJointPositionsInto
fields.doc: Copies the latest joint positions into caller-owned storage without building an observation snapshot.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: Reads the latest published native state without advancing time.

fields.name: publishSensorFrame
fields.doc:
Publishes one observation of an externally sourced sensor (see
`RobotRuntimeSensorBlueprint.isExternalKind`) against its authored mount.
The runtime stamps the authored frame, link, and mount plus the receive
time; later snapshots carry the latest frame for each such sensor.
A `gnss_pose` frame carries latitude and longitude in degrees and ENU yaw
in radians; a `camera` frame carries an image and no values. Tool contact
carries one digital value; force/torque carries XYZ newtons followed by
XYZ newton-metres in the mounted sensor frame; tool vacuum carries one
non-negative kPa value.

fields.name: publishSensorFrameAndGet
fields.doc: Publish and return the exact frame retained by the runtime snapshot.

fields.name: publishCameraFrame
fields.doc: Publishes one camera image; see `publishSensorFrame`.

types.name: RobotRuntimeBlueprint
types.doc:
Immutable-at-execution compiled robot description consumed by RobotRuntime.

Keeping this boundary separate from the editable `robotkit.model.RobotModel`
model makes validation and native handle creation deterministic.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: Semantic mappings are absent only for manually constructed native blueprints.

fields.name: switches
fields.doc: Immutable switch definitions sampled by simulation or supplied by device inputs.

fields.name: cylinderDrives
fields.doc: Cylinder process drives are bound to channels, never to trajectory axes.

fields.name: velocityDrives
fields.doc: Velocity process drives are bound to analog channels, never to trajectory axes.

fields.name: processModelJoints
fields.doc: Coordinates driven by a deterministic process observer, excluded from arm trajectories.

fields.name: selfCollision
fields.doc: MuJoCo self-collision is enabled unless this opt-out is set false.

fields.name: contactPairs
fields.doc: Explicit contacts between linkCollisionShapes entries, by index.

fields.name: observedLimitTolerance
fields.doc:
How far an observed position may pass a joint limit before the runtime
faults; zero keeps limits exact. Legged robots resting on compliant stops
need a small tolerance.

fields.name: floatingBase
fields.doc: True makes the root link a free six-DOF body in Simulation.

Resolve the cushioned stop's force/mass time constant with MuJoCo's two-step floor.

fields.name: processJoints

Sets a tool's channels up with the safe values and stop policy the tool owns (`ToolChannels`). A channel the robot's
setup declared already must say the same, or the tool is refused: a torch's arc cannot be left to keep its output
through a stop because the setup declared it so.

types.name: RuntimeEndpoints
types.doc: Factories for core runtime endpoints. Transport adapters provide their own factories.

types.name: RuntimeJointObservation
types.doc: Owned joint coordinates and their source time from one endpoint observation.

types.name: RuntimeRobotAdapter
types.doc: Shared RobotWorld adapter for runtimes owned either by simulation or a device.

types.name: SimulatedContactSurfaces
types.doc: Shared, explicit contact assumptions for hard machine fixtures and replaceable grip pads.

fields.name: HARD_FIXTURE_TIME_CONSTANT
fields.doc: Matches MuJoCo's 2*dt floor at a 0.25 ms drive substep. This is a simulation assumption.

types.name: SimulatedElectricGripper
types.doc:
Position/effort controlled parallel jaws. Grasp feedback requires contact on both jaws;
a close command or nominal width alone never confirms possession. No kinematic attachment.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (simulation:Simulation, robot:Int, joint:Int, jaws:Array<Int>, openPosition:Float, graspPosition:Float, effort:Float, ?maxSpeed:Float, ?initialPosition:Float):Void

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Position an empty gripper without claiming a grasp.

fields.name: stopAndHold
fields.doc: Leaves the last jaw command energized; a stop must never issue an opening command.

fields.name: commandComplete
fields.doc: Command-ramp completion is an admission condition, never evidence of possession.

types.name: SimulatedHomingSides
types.doc: Resolve home switches to distinct shaft holds in one simulation-owned runtime.

types.name: SimulatedPneumaticGripper
types.doc:
Bridges the logical gripper command to short pulses on the bound cylinder's
two digital valve coils. The physical jaws, workpiece contact and joint switch
remain in the simulation. Contact observations report the free workpiece
between both jaws; they never attach it kinematically.

fields.name: contactLinks
fields.doc: Jaw links derived from the cylinder joint and its mirrored follower.

fields.name: grippedObjects
fields.doc: Free objects supported by both jaws with confirmed width feedback, without a kinematic attachment.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Reset both outputs to the double valve's de-energized, latched state.

types.name: SimulatedPresenceInputAdapter
types.doc: Samples authored cabinet presence inputs from free-object geometry after each physics tick.

types.name: SimulatedRobotZoneAdapter
types.doc:
Samples a controller's `zone_input` sensors after each physics tick, like a safety area scanner:
a zone is occupied while a link of another robot, or a part one of them carries, comes within
`margin` of any of its boxes. The links are their collision hulls and a carried part its simulated shape.
The zone's own machine and parts lying free (the stock in the vise) never occupy it.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (simulation:Simulation, runtime:RobotRuntime, blueprint:RobotRuntimeBlueprint, robotIndex:Int, mechanisms:Array<RobotZoneMechanism>, objects:Array<SimObject>, margin:Float, makeWorld:() -> CollisionWorld):Void

types.name: SimulatedSuctionTool
types.doc:
A suction tool on one link of a simulated robot, worked by its control channel as the valve of a
real ejector is: once the channel is on, it seals on the free object touching the link and the
simulation carries that object on the link; once it is off, it lets go. With nothing under it the
vacuum finds no seal and holds nothing. A tool with a vacuum sensor publishes the vacuum it pulls
there, `sealedKpa` while it holds and none otherwise, so skills tell a grip as they would on a real
robot. Add it to the simulation as a step observer; it acts after each step.

A tool with no channel is worked by `actuate` instead, for scripted playback of a robot that runs
no trajectory plans to carry channel events.

fields.name: REACH
fields.doc: How far from the link an object may be for the vacuum to seal on it, in metres.

fields.name: CLEARANCE
fields.doc:
The gap left between the cup and what it holds. A held object follows its carrier and cannot
yield, so a contact between them would push back on the robot; a gap far above the contact's own
tolerance keeps that force at zero and is invisible at this scale.

fields.name: held
fields.doc: What the tool holds, or null.

fields.name: actuate
fields.doc: Turns a tool with no channel on or off; it seals or lets go after the next step.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: The session reset restored every object and the robot's channels: forget what was held.

fields.name: attach
fields.doc: Attaches an explicitly identified screw or part using the same holding path as contact sealing.

fields.name: placeHeld
fields.doc: Changes the held part's pose through the existing link attachment.

types.name: SimulatedSwitchSensorAdapter
types.doc:
Publish mechanical switch observations after each simulation tick.
The reader supplies actual joint coordinates, including any simulated slip.

fields.name: bindingIndices
fields.doc: Validate before creating a native robot, so bad mounts cannot leave a partial addition.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc:
Reset mechanical history and deterministic repeatability after a robot power cycle.
Publication sequence stays monotonic for existing sensor stream consumers.

types.name: Simulation
types.doc:
The robots taking part in one SimKit session.

The session's owner (Simulation.inSession()'s caller) advances it, alongside
its props and people, and controls its clock (step, start, stop, reset) and
its environment (session objects and actors) directly.

The object creates RobotRuntime handles but remains their simulation owner:
callers should submit through those handles and advance the session once per
tick. It is intentionally separate from SimulatedRobot, which is only a
live Robot adapter for RobotWorld.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Attaches robots to a stopped session the caller owns, steps, and outlives.

fields.name: inSpace
fields.doc: Attaches robots and lets their drives configure the owned physics world.

fields.name: presentFrame
fields.doc: Robot poses from a frame captured from the session.

fields.name: addRobot
fields.doc: Adds topology before the first start or step.

fields.name: addRobotAtPose
fields.doc:
Adds a robot with a resettable 3D pose. Tool padding defaults to a proximity
gap; pass toolMargin to make it physical.

fields.name: ownsRobot
fields.doc: Contacts for a runtime attached to this simulation.

fields.name: supportsContactWrenches
fields.doc: MuJoCo provides solved contact wrenches; the deterministic backend does not model them.

fields.name: sourceTimestampNs
fields.doc:
Logical source time for explicitly stepped sensors. It stays monotonic
across physics resets so published frames remain ordered.

fields.name: virtualDeviceReady
fields.doc: A virtual link is ready only after its device observation and clock qualification.

fields.name: stopVirtualDevice
fields.doc: Deliver device stop before the simulation clock is frozen.

fields.name: setVirtualDeviceInput
fields.doc: Supplies a board-defined numeric input; the explicit peripheral kind owns the input index.

fields.name: virtualDeviceSensor
fields.doc: Latest device sample; sequence zero means no observation has arrived yet.

fields.name: jointSample
fields.doc: Actual physics joint sample, with its own completed-snapshot clock.

fields.name: virtualDeviceChannel
fields.doc: GPIO/analog output already executed by the virtual board.

fields.name: cutVirtualDeviceLink
fields.doc: Injects a virtual RKD6 link loss or reconnects the link.

fields.name: resetRobot
fields.doc:
Restores one robot's initial body pose and runtime state. The session
must be stopped.

fields.name: setPowerUpOffsets
fields.doc:
Configure a stopped cold/reset robot's physical power-up pose and unknown counter origin.
Full coupling-consistent joint vector in SI units; later lost steps use setJointSlip.

fields.name: setPowerUpSides
fields.doc: Cold placement including explicit motor-side racking; retain it across robot reset.

fields.name: setSquaringHold
fields.doc:
Hold one motor-side shaft at a physical SI position while its leader continues.
Release retains follower slip. The homing owner must release on every exit path.

fields.name: homingSides
fields.doc: Create a side controller tied to the runtime owned at this robot index.

fields.name: teleportRobot
fields.doc:
Teleports one robot base while leaving the shared clock untouched. The
session must be stopped.

fields.name: driveRobotBase
fields.doc:
Moves one robot's kinematic base to a pose that takes effect on the next
tick. Unlike teleportRobot, this keeps a realtime clock running, keeps
sensor history, and does not change the pose restored by reset or
resetRobot. The base's velocity over the tick is the motion from its
previous pose, so the IMU measures consecutive drives as continuous
motion. Use it to drive a base every tick; use placeRobotBase for a jump.

fields.name: placeRobotBase
fields.doc:
Jumps one robot's base to a pose for the next tick without stopping a
realtime clock, resetting sensors, or changing the reset pose. The base
keeps its body-frame velocity through the jump, so the IMU sees no spike,
and a differential-drive plant continues from the new pose.

fields.name: setDifferentialDrive
fields.doc:
Couples one robot's wheel velocity targets to its kinematic base. Each
tick the base rolls by the wheel targets the robot applied for that tick
(after runtime clamping, zero after any stop), before physics advances,
whatever submitted them. Joint indices are robot joint indices; lengths
are metres. A wheel's direction is -1 when a positive joint rate rolls it
backward. The plant starts from the base's current pose.

fields.name: clearDifferentialDrive
fields.doc: Removes a robot's differential-drive coupling; the base stays in place.

fields.name: differentialDriveState
fields.doc:
Reads a robot's differential-drive plant after the latest tick: its
planar pose (yaw unwrapped) and the wheel rates the robot applied.

fields.name: setOmniDrive
fields.doc:
Couples one robot's three omni-wheel velocity targets to its kinematic
base, like setDifferentialDrive but decoding a full planar body twist, so
the base can strafe. `wheelAngles` are the wheels' mount angles about +Z
from the base's x axis; see rk_simulation_set_omni_drive.

fields.name: clearOmniDrive
fields.doc: Removes a robot's omni-wheel coupling; the base stays in place.

fields.name: omniDriveState
fields.doc:
Reads a robot's omni-wheel plant after the latest tick: its planar pose
(yaw unwrapped) and the three wheel rates the robot applied.

fields.name: setJointPositions
fields.doc:
Places a robot's joints, in joint order, as a pose to start from (such as
a standing keyframe) while the simulation is stopped. Velocities become
zero; reset returns joints to zero.

fields.name: springProcessJoint
fields.doc:
Makes a process-owned tool joint a passive spring resting at `restPosition`, with `stiffness` and `damping` in the
joint's units (see `rk_simulation_spring_process_joint`).

fields.name: setServoFeedforward
fields.doc: Model-based bias for simulated position/trajectory servo control. Direct servo commands carry their own bias.

fields.name: applyRobotForce
fields.doc:
Pushes a robot's base for the next tick: a world-frame force (N) and
torque (N m) at its centre of mass. Repeat every tick to push for longer.

fields.name: robotPose
fields.doc: Reads one robot base pose without mutating physics or the editable model.

fields.name: robotBaseVelocity
fields.doc:
Reads one robot base's world-frame twist: linear in metres per second,
angular in radians per second. A floating base reports its free motion.

fields.name: linkBody
fields.doc:
The physics body that carries a robot link, to use as the carrier when a session object is held by
that link (`SimSession.holdObject`), for instance a workpiece gripped by a suction cup.

fields.name: stopForTopologyChange
fields.doc: Releases the host between ticks so the next explicit step recompiles a changed joint topology.

fields.name: createObjectScrewJoint
fields.signature: (robotIndex:Int, spindleJointIndex:Int, member:nksim_body, screw:nativekit.sim.SimObject, axisPoint:Array<Float>, axis:Array<Float>, lead:Float, lowerLimit:Float, upperLimit:Float, socketRatio:Float, threadStiffness:Float, threadDampingRatio:Float, advanceArmature:Float):nksim_joint

fields.name: createObjectFixedFollower
fields.doc:
Attaches a dynamic CAD body to a robot link at its current measured pose.
The physics host must be stopped between ticks; destroy the returned joint
at the next docked release to preserve the body's live pose and mass.

fields.name: createObjectMeasuredFixedJoint
fields.doc:
Physically fastens two session objects at their measured pose while stopped.
The session owns the connection and removes it on reset.

fields.name: destroyObjectJoint
fields.doc: Removes one runtime-created object joint while the physics host is stopped.

fields.name: createRobotFixedFollower
fields.doc:
Attach a floating articulated robot root to another robot link without snapping.
The host must be stopped between ticks; a child runtime can have only one mount.

fields.name: createRobotBodyFixedFollower
fields.doc: Attach a floating articulated tool root to a session body, such as its fixed CAD dock, at a stopped tick boundary.

fields.name: destroyRobotJoint
fields.doc: Release an articulated robot mount at a stopped tick boundary, preserving the child's live pose.

fields.name: objectCarrier
fields.doc: The native body carrying an environment object, or zero while free.

fields.name: objectPose
fields.doc: Where a session object is now.

fields.name: holdObjectOnLink
fields.doc: Carries a session object on a robot link at `relative`, its pose in the link's frame, until released.

fields.name: releaseObject
fields.doc: Lets go of a session object some link carries.

fields.name: unbindObjectFromLink
fields.doc: Stops attributing a session object's contact load to its former robot carrier.

fields.name: holdObjectOnObject
fields.doc: Retains a part in an identified environment object's body frame.

fields.name: objectBody
fields.doc: The physics body belonging to an identified environment object.

fields.name: linkPose
fields.doc: Reads an articulated link pose without mutating the simulation.

fields.name: excludeContactPair
fields.doc: Excludes one robot link from one free scene object for this session's physics.

fields.name: capturePresentation
fields.doc: Copies every presentation body pose under one native simulation lock.

fields.name: rejection
fields.doc:
RobotKit's status for the robot fault that failed the latest tick, such
as RK_ERROR_LIMIT, or RK_OK. The session that stepped reports only that a
participant failed.

types.name: SimulationClosure
types.doc: Closed assembly edge between two links in an existing tree.

types.name: SimulationCollisionPacking
types.doc: Pack exact convex geometry into the existing native hull buffer when primitive slots run out.

types.name: SimulationDifferentialDriveState
types.doc: Differential-drive plant state; see Simulation.differentialDriveState.

types.name: SimulationEndpoints
types.doc:
Factories for simulation-owned cyclic and virtual scheduled endpoints.
The shared Simulation constructs and drives their native owners.

types.name: SimulationHarness
types.doc:
Test/standalone convenience that owns a SimulationSpace and the Simulation
joined to it end to end: construction, clock control (step, start, stop,
reset), and simple box environment objects, mirroring the deleted
self-owned rk_simulation mode for callers, mainly tests, that just want one
thing to construct, step, and dispose. Production code should own a
SimulationSpace and session directly and drive them itself, as the app
(ApplicationSimulation, SimulationSpace) does.

fields.name: step
fields.doc:
Advances the session one tick and notifies the simulation's step
observers. A tick the robots refused throws with RobotKit's status.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: Stops realtime stepping but leaves the harness available for disposal.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Restores every body and the fixed-step clock to the editable-scene state.

fields.name: resetRobot
fields.doc:
Restores one robot's initial body pose and runtime state. Stops first:
the session must be stopped for this edit, as it must for Simulation's.

fields.name: teleportRobot
fields.doc:
Teleports one robot base while leaving the shared clock untouched.
Stops first: the session must be stopped for this edit.

fields.name: spawnPlane
fields.doc:
Adds an infinite static ground plane through `position` (default the
origin), facing the +Z axis of `rotation` (default the world XY plane).

fields.name: spawnBox
fields.doc: Adds a box to the shared physics world and returns its owned session object.

fields.name: removeObject
fields.doc: Removes an environment object from the shared scene and physics world.

fields.name: teleportObject
fields.doc: Teleports an environment object and clears its velocity.

fields.name: objectPose
fields.doc: Reads an environment body's latest physics pose.

types.name: SimulationObjectFixture
types.doc: Retains an identified environment body on a live fixture and reports its actual native ownership.

fields.name: retainRigid
fields.doc: Final rigid retention at the measured pose; dynamic fixtures must retain the member's physical mass.

fields.name: releaseRigid
fields.doc: Release this fixture's retained body at its measured pose for a qualified continuation.

fields.name: threadedBody
fields.doc: The native body a fastener threads into: the member's own, or its robot link's.

types.name: SimulationOmniDriveState
types.doc: Omni-wheel plant state; see Simulation.omniDriveState.

types.name: SimulationPresentationPose
types.doc: One immutable body pose copied from a shared simulation presentation.

types.name: SimulationPresentationSnapshot
types.doc: Owned, immutable native presentation copied at one simulation revision.

fields.name: linkPose
fields.doc: Constant-time view of an already captured robot link pose.

types.name: SimulationSolver
types.doc:
Solver choices for a session's world (SimWorldOptions.integrator and
frictionCone, as SimulationSpace and SimulationHarness take them), matching
SimKit's integrator and friction-cone values.

types.name: SimulationSpace
types.doc:
The scene, physics world, and SimKit session one simulation runs in.
Robots (through Simulation.inSpace()), environment props, and people all
join the session. Shared by the app and by anything else that needs to own
a session end to end, such as a test.

fields.name: DETERMINISTIC
fields.doc: The deterministic, dependency-free test backend.

fields.name: MUJOCO
fields.doc: The MuJoCo backend; must be built in.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Backend selected when this space was created; sensor contracts use it to reject unsupported observations.

fields.name: create
fields.doc:
Creates a space on the deterministic test backend or on MuJoCo. Physics
advances `physicsSubsteps` times per tick; `solver` picks the integrator,
friction cone, and solver iteration limits (unset keeps backend defaults).

fields.name: requireDrives
fields.doc: Derives integration from the drive loops and their mechanical loads.

fields.name: requireInterval
fields.doc: Steps the world at least this finely (a spring integrated explicitly, a stiff cushion), and implicitly.

fields.name: requireContact
fields.doc: Resolves authored positive contact time constants without MuJoCo's two-step safety floor changing them.

fields.name: requireStops
fields.doc: Joint stops have the same two-step resolution requirement as shape contacts.

fields.name: dispose
fields.doc: Releases the session, then the world it borrowed, then the scene.

types.name: SimulationStepObserver
types.doc:
Called after an explicit Simulation.step or its owning SimSession.step
with a monotonic logical source time.

types.name: StepTicks
types.doc:
The least whole number of step-tick periods between two steps: what an
RKD6 device enforces (`min_step_ticks`). The host chooses it once, from
a step frequency it actually has (an actuator's authored speed in steps,
a driver's step-rate ceiling), and derives every rate from it; nothing
turns a rate back into ticks, so float rounding can never cost a tick.

fields.name: forLimit
fields.doc: The ticks for at most `stepsPerSecond` (null: no limit but the tick itself).

fields.name: rate
fields.doc: The rate, in units per second, a device stepping every `ticks` reaches with `stepsPerUnit` (already `wire`).

fields.name: wire
fields.doc:
Steps per unit as the wire carries them (f32). The binding quantises its steps per unit here once and
plans, deploys and checks with that value, so no later stage has to mirror the device's rounding.

types.name: SwitchDriveBinding
types.doc: Convert a switch side's observed drive shaft into its monitored axis coordinate.

types.name: VirtualActuatorOptions
types.doc: One ordered RKD6 channel and its SimpleTransmission into a model joint.

fields.name: minStepTicks
fields.doc: The least whole step-tick periods between steps (`StepTicks`).

fields.name: holdStiffness
fields.doc:
How stiffly the actuator holds the joint it measures, in that joint's coordinate (N/m or N m/rad), and the inertia
that joint turns, kg or kg m^2: a stepper that drives a compliant coupling holds its pulley with its torque-angle
stiffness. Zero stiffness keeps the simulation's default position loop.

fields.name: holdDamping
fields.doc: The critical damping of the hold on the inertia it carries.

fields.name: holdInterval
fields.doc: The longest physics step the hold's spring is stable under (it is integrated explicitly), seconds; infinite without one.

types.name: VirtualDeviceOptions
types.doc: Optional in-process RKD6 device and simulated UART for Simulation.addRobot.

fields.name: peripheralKind
fields.doc: Board-defined profile data; process owners supply its meaning.

fields.name: externalSensorSlots
fields.doc: Numeric slots published through authored external sensors, excluded from the native sensor layout.

fields.name: controller
fields.doc: The virtual board's unique id, 32 hex digits, which a deployment names; "Virtual-Device-1" by default.

types.name: VirtualHeaters
types.doc:
The heaters of a virtual RKD6 device: the board runs the controller code it would run on hardware (PID, watchdog,
safe state) against a lumped thermal plant, and this class configures it, publishes what it reports to the runtime's
`tool_heater` sensors, and lets an experiment reach the plant (a disconnected element, a thermistor that has fallen
off, a draught).

fields.name: ELEMENT
fields.doc: `input` kinds of `setInput`.

fields.name: configure
fields.doc: Sets up the board's heater profile (peripheral 2) and the sensor slots it feeds; before the robot is added.

fields.name: observe
fields.doc: Publishes the device's latest report of each heater to its sensor, and returns the readings.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: The robot's board was restarted (a new session): publication restarts from nothing.

fields.name: setInput
fields.doc: Reaches the plant of heater `name`: see the kinds above.

types.name: VirtualInputOptions
types.doc: A physical virtual switch bound to an actuator's actual step counter.

types.name: VirtualServoOptions
types.doc: Servo emulation on the virtual board's pulse grid; physical stepper wiring stays in DeviceBinding.

fields.name: ACCELERATION_SCALE
fields.doc: Reserve 2% of acceleration for clock fitting (up to 0.5% rate error) and float polynomial conversion.

types.name: LoadSafetyConfiguration
types.doc: Tunable soft-limit reductions used by load-aware safety policy.

types.name: LoadSafetyPolicy
types.doc: Applies load- and fork-height-dependent soft limits to one mobile forklift.

fields.name: refresh
fields.doc: Reads the latest fork and load state, updates MobileBase caps, and returns a snapshot.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Returns the last policy result; call refresh at the application's control frequency.

types.name: Safety
types.doc: User-facing safety state source; native RobotRuntime enforces hard limits and stops.

types.name: SafetyPhase
types.doc: User-visible operating condition reported by safety policy.

types.name: SafetyRestriction
types.doc: Active high-level policy restriction; hard enforcement remains in RobotRuntime.

types.name: SafetyState
types.doc: Immutable operator-facing state and restrictions reported by safety policy.

fields.name: effectiveMotionLimits
fields.doc: Dynamic user-level motion cap when this state comes from a policy.

fields.name: footprint
fields.doc: Conservative planar robot-and-load footprint when geometry is known.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (phase:SafetyPhase, speedLimitMetersPerSecond:Float, stoppingEnvelope:StoppingEnvelope, restrictions:Array<SafetyRestriction>, sourceTimestampNs:Int64, receivedTimestampNs:Int64, sourceClockId:String, receivedClockId:String, ?effectiveMotionLimits:MotionLimits, ?footprint:Footprint):Void

types.name: StoppingEnvelope
types.doc: Conservative one-dimensional stopping distance from speed, latency, and deceleration.

types.name: SerialRobot
types.doc:
RobotWorld adapter that owns and starts a serial runtime for one board, wired to the model's
actuators by a device layout.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (id:RobotId, model:RobotModel, profile:robotkit.profile.RobotProfile, devicePath:String, controllerHex:String, layout:DeviceLayout, maxTargetError:Float, ?baud:Int, ?ownerPeriodNs:haxe.Int64, ?processingAllowanceNs:haxe.Int64, ?channels:Array<ProcessChannelDeclaration>, ?stepTickHz:Int, ?linkLossTimeoutNs:haxe.Int64, ?clockSyncBoundNs:haxe.Int64):Void

types.name: SerialRuntimeEndpoint
types.doc: Factory for a serial generation-6 endpoint; transport selection stays outside RobotRuntime.

fields.name: create
fields.doc:
Creates a serial runtime for the board `controllerHex` (its 32-digit unique id) wired as
`binding` says, within an SI-unit error budget. The blueprint should be compiled from the
binding's model so its limits are the device's. The board must be that controller and agree
with the configuration, or this throws with the device's reason on stderr.

fields.name: createRuntime
fields.doc: Create a runtime with its physical device switches published during observation.

fields.name: identify
fields.doc: Reads the unique id (32 lowercase hex digits) of the board on a serial port.

types.name: SimulatedRobot
types.doc: RobotWorld adapter over a runtime owned by an externally managed Simulation.

types.name: Charge
types.doc: Docks at a detected charging target and waits for the requested battery charge.

types.name: Dock
types.doc: Plans and navigates to the approach pose of a detected docking target.

fields.name: blockedTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc: Forwarded to the approach GoTo; see GoTo.blockedTimeoutSeconds.

types.name: FollowPath
types.doc: Tracks a caller-supplied path without planning or replanning it.

types.name: GoTo
types.doc: Plans, follows, and replans a route to a framed goal.

fields.name: observePerception
fields.doc:
Converts one robot observation into obstacles in the Navigator costmap
frame. The provider should update the Navigator's localization from the
same observation before returning.

fields.name: blockedTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc:
Longest continuous time, in update durations, that the Navigator may stay
Blocked before the skill fails with the blocked reason. The Navigator keeps
retrying its route plan within this window.

types.name: HandlePart
types.doc:
Picks a part up with a tool, or sets the held part down. `contact` gives, in the map frame,
where the tool meets: the part's grasp point to pick, or where its contact must be for the held part
to rest on its seat to place. Optional `orientation` gives the tool rotation in the same map frame;
omission leaves spin free. Both are read when the skill starts, so they follow the part wherever it
is; the robot's place comes from `localization`, and its base must stand still meanwhile. The arm's
program switches the tool's channel on the robot, as it would a real ejector valve. With the tool's
grasp sensor the skill tells the outcome as a real cell does: picking succeeds when the sensor reads
at least `holdThreshold` afterwards, placing when it reads less; without one it trusts the program.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (runner:HandlingRunner, localization:Localization, contact:() -> Vec3, hold:Bool, ?graspSensor:String, ?holdThreshold:Float, ?orientation:() -> Quat, ?approach:() -> Vec3):Void

types.name: HandlingRunner
types.doc:
Arm motion for picking a part up and setting it down. RobotKit names the motion; MotionKit
implements it (`motionkit.robot.HandlingPlanRunner`), so RobotKit itself stays free of MotionKit,
as with `SurfacePlanRunner`.

fields.name: run
fields.doc:
Brings the tool's contact to `contact`, in the arm's base frame, from `approach`;
switches the tool's hold channel to `hold` there and rises again. Without an explicit
orientation it returns to the home pose; with one it stays at the raised pose, preserving a
held part for the next operation. A missing approach uses the conventional base +Z direction.

types.name: PickPallet
types.doc: Plans to a pallet approach, positions forks, and waits for secured-load confirmation.

fields.name: blockedTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc: Forwarded to the approach GoTo; see GoTo.blockedTimeoutSeconds.

fields.name: new

fields.doc: Hamilton product: applies `other` after this rotation (this * other).

types.doc:
Immutable rigid transform: translation (meters) plus a unit quaternion

coordinates expressed in frame `b` into frame `a`; composition follows

fields.name: compose
fields.doc: `this.compose(local)`: if this is `a_T_b` and local is `b_T_c`, returns `a_T_c`.

fields.name: transformPoint

fields.name: transformVector

fields.name: transformTwist
fields.doc:
Adjoint action: moves a twist expressed in this transform's local frame
into its parent frame. If this is `a_T_b`, a twist known in `b` becomes
the equivalent twist in `a`.

fields.name: transformWrench

fields.name: integrate

First-order integration of a body-frame twist over `dt`: composes this
transform with the small motion the twist produces in its own frame.

types.name: ConvexDistance
types.doc:
The distance between two convex hulls, from their corners: the Gilbert-Johnson-Keerthi algorithm. It looks for the point of
the Minkowski difference of the two hulls nearest the origin, by repeatedly taking the difference's extreme point toward
the origin and finding the nearest point of the small simplex they make. A hull is its corners (any points whose hull it is),
a few dozen for a part's collision hull, so a query costs a few hundred operations however big the parts are.

The distance is exact for hulls that are apart. Hulls that touch or overlap give zero (how deep they overlap is not worked
out). When a separating plane shows the hulls are farther apart than `enough`, the search stops with that plane's gap, a lower
bound of the distance: the caller asking whether bodies keep a margin need not know more.

fields.name: between
fields.doc: `a` and `b` are corners as x, y, z triples in one frame.

types.name: ConvexSolid
types.doc:
A convex solid made from the vertices of its hull, for geometric questions the physics engine's
contacts do not answer: how far a point is from it, and where a ray enters it. It keeps the
hull as outward planes, so both questions cost one pass over them.

Planes come from every triple of vertices that has all the others on one side, so a hull of up to
`EXACT_LIMIT` vertices is exact; a larger one is replaced by its bounding box, which only errs
on the safe side of "the work is at least this big".

fields.name: EXACT_LIMIT
fields.doc: Hulls with more vertices than this are boxed (the triple search is cubic).

fields.name: DYKSTRA_SWEEPS
fields.doc: The most sweeps over the planes the nearest-point search makes.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `vertices` is x, y, z per vertex, in the solid's own frame.

fields.name: box
fields.doc: The bounding box of `min` to `max`, as a solid.

fields.name: cornerPoints
fields.doc: The solid's corners, as x, y, z triples in its own frame.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc:
How far the point is outside the solid: negative inside (how deep, to the nearest face), zero on the surface. Outside
it is the true distance to the solid. In front of a face that is the face plane's distance, found at once when the
point's projection on that plane lies in the solid; beside an edge or at a corner (where the largest plane distance
falls short, to 0.71 or 0.58 of the truth at its worst) it is found by projecting on the planes in turn with
Dykstra's corrections, which converges to the nearest point of the intersection of the half-spaces.

fields.name: ray
fields.signature: (ox:Float, oy:Float, oz:Float, dx:Float, dy:Float, dz:Float, range:Float):Float
fields.doc:
Where the ray from `o` along the unit vector `d` first meets the solid: the distance along it, zero when it starts
inside, or positive infinity when it misses or the solid is farther than `range`.

types.name: Gripper
types.doc: Two-state gripper controls and observed grasp outcome.

types.doc:
One logical jaw command. It defaults open on a fault and retains its value
through an ordinary stop so a stopped arm keeps the part it is carrying.

types.name: HeaterChannels
types.doc:
The channels a heater is worked by: its target, in degrees Celsius, and optionally the part-cooling fan that blows on
it (a duty from 0 to 1). Both are zero when the outputs are made safe, so a fault or an emergency stop switches them
off. The target keeps its value through a commanded stop or an aborted motion: pausing a print does not cool the
hotend, and a held temperature is the controller's to hold. The fan keeps its duty too.

types.name: HeaterSensor
types.doc:
The `tool_heater` sensor: one frame of five values in a fixed order, so a reading is one consistent snapshot of
the controller. The controller owns the heater (PID, a runaway watchdog, a safe state): the host sets a target on
the heater's analog channel and reads this frame back.

leaks, cup deformation or load sharing among several cups.

The channel a suction tool is worked by, with its safe value and stop policy. It keeps its output through a commanded
stop or an aborted motion, so a robot that stops (or whose base arrives somewhere) does not drop what it holds; a
fault or an emergency stop still takes it to off. The opposite of a welder's (`WeldChannels`).

types.doc:
One sealed suction contact. Local +Z points from the cup toward the part.
Vacuum is a guaranteed minimum measured at the cup; friction and moment
rating must describe this cup and workpiece surface at that vacuum.

A tool that works against a standoff distance from a work surface and can
be turned on/off for a process. Commands carry the caller's timestamp

center point relative to the flange frame, per ARCHITECTURE.md's

The mission owns dock motion and CAD-body attachment; it may advance this
transaction only after those physical stages have completed.

take it to, while a commanded stop keeps a closed gripper closed on its part.
